FL.summary: The ACLU of Florida condemned HB 991, warning that its proof-of-citizenship requirements and removal of student IDs as acceptable identification would disenfranchise eligible voters, particularly students and seniors.

GA.title: Fuller, Harris advance to special election runoff in Georgia's 14th District
GA.summary: Republican Clay Fuller and Democrat Shawn Harris advanced to an April 7 runoff in the special election to replace former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene in Georgia's 14th Congressional District, with neither candidate securing a majority in the March 10 vote.

GA.title: Crowded field emerges in race to decide who will be Georgia's next governor
GA.summary: Candidate qualifying wrapped up at the state Capitol for Georgia's May 19 primary, with a crowded field vying for the open governor's seat as the state prepares for its first competitive gubernatorial election cycle in years.

GA.title: State Election Board pushes for faster action on shift away from QR codes on Georgia ballots
GA.summary: Georgia's State Election Board unanimously passed a resolution urging lawmakers to accelerate the transition to hand-marked paper ballots, a day after legislators unveiled SB 214 which would delay the switch from QR-coded ballots until the 2028 elections.

GA.title: Local election workers ready for midterms as lawmakers ponder big changes to Georgia's voting system
GA.summary: As Georgia's legislative session nears its end, election workers are preparing for 2026 midterms while lawmakers debate proposals to overhaul the state's voting system, including a potential switch from touchscreen machines to hand-marked paper ballots by 2028.

GA.title: Georgia Senate votes for rapid move to hand-marked paper ballots before November elections
GA.summary: The Georgia Senate voted to push for implementing hand-marked paper ballots before the November 2026 elections, in contrast to a House proposal that would delay the transition until 2028.

HI.title: Hawaii Office of Elections March 2026 newsletter addresses citizenship verification rumors
HI.summary: The Hawaii Office of Elections issued a newsletter clarifying that voters are not required to provide proof of U.S. citizenship to register or vote, countering recent rumors, and stated it is monitoring potential federal election law changes.

ID.title: Idaho's Republican state officials are all running for re-election
ID.summary: All of Idaho's Republican statewide officeholders have filed for re-election ahead of the May 19 primary, with candidate filing for federal, statewide, and legislative offices closing on March 13.

ID.title: Here are the Idaho statewide candidates who have filed to run in the 2026 election
ID.summary: The Idaho Capital Sun compiled a full list of statewide candidates who filed to run in 2026, as candidate filing for federal and statewide offices closed on March 13 ahead of the May 19 primary election.

IL.title: Juliana Stratton wins Illinois Democratic Senate primary
IL.summary: Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton won the Democratic primary for the U.S. Senate seat being vacated by retiring Sen. Dick Durbin, defeating Reps. Raja Krishnamoorthi and Robin Kelly in the March 17 primary with support from Gov. JB Pritzker.

IL.title: 2026 Illinois primary results set up Pritzker vs. Bailey governor rematch
IL.summary: The March 17 Illinois primary set up a rematch between Gov. JB Pritzker and Republican Darren Bailey for governor, while Don Tracy won the GOP Senate nomination to face Stratton in November.

IL.title: Supreme Court weighs whether to limit mail ballot counts after Election Day and its impact on Illinois
IL.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court is considering a case that could limit whether states can count mail-in ballots received after Election Day, with potential implications for Illinois voters who rely on extended mail ballot receipt deadlines.

IN.title: State argues against allowing college student IDs for voting
IN.summary: Indiana state attorneys filed a 43-page memorandum opposing a preliminary injunction against the student ID voting ban (SB 10), arguing the law does not burden the right to vote and that only a small number of voters would be affected.

IN.title: Indiana's 2026 primary: Who's running for congressional and legislative seats
IN.summary: WFYI published a comprehensive guide to Indiana's 2026 primary election, covering all nine U.S. House seats, 100 Indiana House seats, and 25 Indiana Senate seats on the May 5 ballot.

IN.title: Indiana voter registration open through April 6 for May primary
IN.summary: Indiana officials reminded voters that the registration deadline for the May 5, 2026 primary election is April 6, with early in-person voting set to begin April 7 at county clerk offices across the state.

IA.title: Iowa Secretary of State releases final list of 2026 primary candidates
IA.summary: Iowa Secretary of State Paul Pate released the finalized list of nearly 300 Democratic and Republican candidates who qualified for the June 2 primary ballot, following the March 13 candidate filing deadline.

IA.title: Here's what advanced and failed in the Iowa Legislature's second deadline of 2026
IA.summary: Iowa lawmakers hit their second major legislative deadline on March 20, narrowing the pool of bills still eligible for debate, with most measures needing to have cleared a committee in the opposite chamber to survive.

KS.title: Kansas House passes election bills restricting early voting and mail-in ballots
KS.summary: The Kansas House passed HB 2569 (78-45) and HB 2437 (80-43), with Democrats warning the bills represent voter suppression while Republicans argued they strengthen election integrity.

KS.title: Kansas Legislature passes package of elections bills that alter voting processes
KS.summary: The Kansas Legislature passed HB 2437 (SAVE Kansas Act, mandating SAVE database voter roll verification) and HB 2569 (which could eliminate no-excuse mail-in voting if signature verification laws are struck down), with both bills falling short of veto-proof majorities.

KS.title: ACLU of Kansas condemns lawmakers' attack on voting rights
KS.summary: The ACLU of Kansas issued a statement condemning the passage of HB 2437 and HB 2569, calling the legislation an unprecedented attack on Kansans' voting rights that could disenfranchise eligible voters.

KY.title: Here's a look at who's running and what's at stake in Kentucky's 2026 elections
KY.summary: WDRB published a comprehensive overview of Kentucky's 2026 elections, covering the open U.S. Senate race following Mitch McConnell's retirement, all 100 Kentucky House seats, half the Senate seats, and Louisville's first nonpartisan mayoral election.

KY.title: 4 takeaways from the money race for U.S. Senate in Kentucky
KY.summary: As Kentucky's May 19 primary approaches, campaign finance reports reveal the state of the race to replace retiring Senate leader Mitch McConnell, with Andy Barr, Daniel Cameron, and Nate Morris leading in fundraising on the Republican side.

KY.title: Kentucky elections bill would increase donor limits, restrict forms of voter ID
KY.summary: A Kentucky elections bill moving through the legislature would increase campaign donor limits and restrict acceptable forms of voter ID, removing Social Security cards and public benefit cards from the list of secondary identification documents.

LA.title: Louisiana State Legislative Special Election Runoffs Held March 14
LA.summary: Voters in New Orleans and St. Bernard Parish went to the polls in special election runoffs to fill vacant state legislative seats, including a Senate District 3 runoff between Democrats Kenn Barnes and Sidney Barthelemy II.

LA.title: Bill Advances to Remove BESE Elections from Closed Primary System
LA.summary: A bill to remove Board of Elementary and Secondary Education elections from Louisiana's new closed party primary system advanced in committee, potentially saving the state $5.4 million in standalone primary election costs.

LA.title: Secretary of State Nancy Landry Talks Election Security
LA.summary: Secretary of State Nancy Landry discussed a trio of election security bills for the 2026 session, including HB 691 to cross-reference voter rolls with a federal citizenship verification database, and plans to replace Louisiana's 30-year-old voting machines.

ME.title: Dem AG Says Maine's RCV Expansion Violates State Constitution
ME.summary: Analysis of Maine Attorney General Aaron Frey's legal brief arguing that LD 1666, the bill to expand ranked-choice voting to gubernatorial and state legislative elections, violates the Maine Constitution's plurality requirement.

ME.title: Maine 2026 Poll: Platner Leads Gov. Mills, Democrats Lead Sen. Collins
ME.summary: An Emerson College poll found Platner leading Mills 55-28 in the Democratic primary, and both Democratic candidates leading Collins in general election matchups, with Collins holding a net 30-point unfavorable rating among independents.

ME.title: Hoping to Unseat Collins, Maine Democrats Battle It Out in an Expensive U.S. Senate Primary
ME.summary: Governor Janet Mills and oyster farmer Graham Platner are engaged in a heated Democratic primary battle to challenge Republican Senator Susan Collins, with Platner leading in polls 55% to 28%.

ME.title: Janet Mills and Graham Platner Battle for Female Voters in Maine's Key Senate Race
ME.summary: Both Democratic Senate candidates launched TV ads and events targeting women voters ahead of the June 9 primary, as the group could be decisive in both the primary and the November general election against Collins.

MD.title: Maryland House Attempts to Revive Congressional Redistricting, Senate Remains Opposed
MD.summary: Maryland House Democrats made another attempt to advance congressional redistricting to flip the state's sole GOP-held seat, but Senate President Bill Ferguson continued to block the effort, calling the latest proposal a "nonstarter."

MD.title: Senate Leader Calls Latest Redistricting Effort from House a Nonstarter
MD.summary: Senate President Bill Ferguson rejected House amendments to a legislative vacancy bill that included language enabling future congressional redistricting, killing the latest Democratic effort to redraw districts before the 2026 midterms.

MA.title: Gov. Healey Says Proposed Rent Control Ballot Question Is Already Having an Effect
MA.summary: Governor Healey urged voters to reject the rent control and income tax reduction ballot questions headed for the November 2026 ballot, saying the rent control proposal alone has already halted some housing developments and caused developers to lose funding.

MA.title: Healey Urges Voters to Reject Rent Control, Income Tax-Cut Ballot Questions
MA.summary: Governor Healey publicly opposed two of the most prominent 2026 ballot measures, saying rent control would discourage housing development and the income tax cut would reduce state revenue, while expressing support for a public records access proposal.

MA.title: Special State Election in 5th Essex Representative District
MA.summary: A special general election is scheduled for March 31, 2026, in the 5th Essex District (Essex, Rockport, Manchester-by-the-Sea, Gloucester) to fill the seat left vacant after the death of Rep. Ann-Margaret Ferrante.

MI.title: Senate Passes Bipartisan Legislation to Move Michigan Primary Date
MI.summary: The Michigan Senate passed bipartisan legislation to move the state's primary election from August to May starting in 2028, aiming to give election clerks more time to prepare between the primary and general election.

MI.title: Michigan Democrats Formally Oppose Voter ID Ballot Proposal, Calling It 'Voter Suppression'
MI.summary: Michigan Democrats officially opposed the Americans for Citizen Voting ballot initiative that would require proof of citizenship to register and verify citizenship of all registered voters, calling it voter suppression.

MI.title: Anthony Forlini wins Republican nomination for Michigan secretary of state
MI.summary: Macomb County Clerk Anthony Forlini was selected by Michigan Republicans at their endorsement convention to be their secretary of state candidate in 2026, winning 55% of the first-ballot vote.

MI.title: Moving Primary Election to May Advances as Michigan Senate Passes Bills
MI.summary: The Michigan Senate passed bills to move primary elections from August to May beginning in 2028, aligning Michigan with 11 other states including Ohio and Indiana that hold May primaries.

MN.title: Minnesota Township Elections Held March 10
MN.summary: Township elections were held across Minnesota on March 10, with voters electing township board members and deciding local issues at annual meetings.

MN.title: Rep. Emmer Cosponsors Minnesota Voter Integrity Act of 2026
MN.summary: U.S. Rep. Tom Emmer (R-MN) cosponsored federal legislation targeting Minnesota's election practices, including a bill by Rep. Pete Stauber to withhold federal election funding if the state doesn't provide voter records.

MN.title: Minnesota Secretary of State Publishes Adopted Election Administration Rules
MN.summary: The Secretary of State published adopted rules in the state register modifying voter registration, ballot formatting, absentee ballot administration, ballot safeguard procedures, and election official training requirements.

MN.title: A Look at Election Measures Up at the Capitol Ahead of 2026
MN.summary: Minnesota lawmakers are considering new election measures including increased penalties for election intimidation, new "I voted" sticker designs, and limiting access to campaign finance addresses ahead of the 2026 midterms.

MN.title: Voters Could Receive Statewide General Election Official Voting Guides by 2027
MN.source: Minnesota House of Representatives Session Daily
MN.summary: The House Elections Committee considered HF3862, which would require the Secretary of State to mail voter guides to every household with a registered voter at least 53 days before each statewide general election, making Minnesota the 33rd state to do so.

MS.title: Hyde-Smith, Colom Head to Mississippi General Election
MS.summary: Following the March 10 primary, Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democratic challenger Scott Colom advanced to the November general election, where they will also face independent candidate Ty Pinkins.

MS.title: Supreme Court Sounds Skeptical of Mississippi Law Allowing Late-Arriving Ballots
MS.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court heard arguments in a case challenging Mississippi's law allowing mail-in ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted if received up to five days later, with justices appearing skeptical of the practice.

MO.title: Judge Again Hears Arguments Over Signatures on Missouri Redistricting Referendum
MO.summary: A judge heard renewed arguments over the validity of signatures collected for the redistricting referendum, as opponents sought to block the measure from reaching the November ballot.

MO.title: Missouri Anti-Redistricting Campaign Has Signatures to Force Vote on New Map
MO.summary: The People Not Politicians campaign announced it has gathered enough verified signatures across all required congressional districts to place a referendum on the November ballot challenging the GOP-drawn congressional map that aims to flip a Kansas City Democratic seat.

MO.title: Missouri Redistricting Referendum Has Enough Verified Signatures for the Ballot
MO.summary: People Not Politicians Missouri released data showing at least 102% of required valid signatures in the final congressional district needed to qualify the redistricting referendum for the November ballot, with over 305,000 total signatures submitted.

MO.title: Missouri Supreme Court Throws Out Voter Registration Restrictions, Keeps Voter Photo ID
MO.summary: The Missouri Supreme Court struck down parts of a 2022 election law that restricted voter registration drives as unconstitutional limits on free speech, while keeping the voter photo ID requirement intact due to standing issues.

MO.title: Missouri Supreme Court Upholds Legislature's Redistricting Authority, Keeps Voter ID Law
MO.summary: In a set of three major rulings, the Missouri Supreme Court upheld the legislature's authority to redraw congressional districts mid-decade, struck down voter registration restrictions on civic groups, and left the photo ID law in place.

MT.title: Montana GOP Infighting Roils 2026 Legislative Primaries
MT.summary: At least 24 Republican incumbents face primary challengers in Montana legislative races, driven by a split between hardline conservatives and moderates over property taxes, with key battles in Senate District 9 and House District 34.

MT.title: More Than 300 File for MT Legislature: Six Initial Takeaways
MT.summary: Over 300 candidates filed for the Montana Legislature by the March 5 deadline, with notable developments including extensive GOP intra-party challenges and two candidates in Cascade County claiming to be Democrats that local party leadership called a hoax.

MT.title: Two Candidates in Cascade County Claim to Be Democrats; Local Party Leadership Says That's a Hoax
MT.summary: Two candidates filed for Montana legislative seats as Democrats in Cascade County, but the local Democratic party said neither individual is a member, raising concerns about deceptive candidate filings.

MT.title: A Montana Senator Declines Re-Election Run, Opening Door for an Independent Candidate
MT.summary: Sen. Steve Daines' surprise withdrawal from the 2026 race and endorsement of U.S. Attorney Kurt Alme has opened the door for independent candidate Seth Bodnar, a former Green Beret and University of Montana president, who argues the last-minute switch undermines Montana voters.

NE.title: 129 candidates running for 42 Nebraska statewide offices in 2026
NE.summary: Filing closed for Nebraska's May 12 primary with 129 candidates for 42 statewide offices including governor, U.S. Senate, three U.S. House seats, and all constitutional officers.

NE.title: No 2026 rerun: Charles Herbster will not run for Nebraska governor
NE.summary: Agribusinessman Charles Herbster announced he will not seek the Republican nomination for governor in 2026, reducing the GOP primary field as incumbent Jim Pillen seeks a second term.

NE.title: Evnen removes Nebraska Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Burbank from ballot
NE.summary: Nebraska Secretary of State Bob Evnen removed Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Cindy Burbank from the primary ballot after the state Republican Party filed a complaint arguing she was not a good-faith candidate.

NE.title: Nebraska Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Burbank stays off ballot after lawsuit dismissal — for now
NE.summary: A Lancaster County District Court judge dismissed Burbank's lawsuit challenging her removal from the primary ballot, though her attorneys announced plans to appeal to the Nebraska Supreme Court.

NE.title: Court orders Nebraska candidate back on U.S. Senate ballot, says Evnen acted late
NE.summary: The Nebraska Supreme Court ruled that Secretary of State Evnen missed the deadline to consider complaints and ordered Cindy Burbank restored to the May primary ballot.

NV.title: Who's running? Hundreds launch campaigns in Nevada 2026 candidate filing period
NV.summary: Nevada's non-judicial candidate filing period opened on March 2 for the June 9 primary, with over 230 candidates filing on the first day including races for governor, U.S. Senate, and congressional seats.

NV.title: Candidate filing ends with a congressional throng, a smattering of perennials, and a couple Fords
NV.summary: Nevada's candidate filing period closed with 27 candidates running for the 2nd Congressional District vacated by retiring Rep. Mark Amodei, including 15 Republicans and 11 Democrats.

NV.title: What to know after Nevada's 2026 candidate filing period wrapped
NV.summary: Summary of Nevada's completed filing period highlighting key races including the crowded 2nd Congressional District, gubernatorial contest, and ballot measures on voter ID and abortion rights heading to November.

NV.title: Las Vegas democratic socialists aim to put 'people over profits' in Assembly primaries
NV.summary: Democratic Socialists of America candidates in Las Vegas are challenging incumbent Democrats in multiple state Assembly primary races ahead of the June 9, 2026 primary election.

NH.title: Republicans vote to end use of school IDs for NH elections
NH.summary: The New Hampshire Senate passed HB 323 on a 16-8 party-line vote to ban the use of college and high school student IDs as voter identification, sending the bill to Governor Kelly Ayotte's desk.

NH.title: Bill to bar student ID cards to prove voter identity heads to Ayotte's desk
NH.summary: HB 323, which would eliminate school-issued identification cards as acceptable voter ID at polls, passed the NH legislature and awaits Governor Ayotte's signature, with Democrats warning it will suppress young voter turnout.

NH.title: What you need to know about voting in NH town elections
NH.summary: A guide for voters ahead of March 10 town elections outlining photo ID requirements, same-day registration procedures, and the new proof-of-citizenship documentation requirements for first-time registrants under HB 1569.

NH.title: Town elections are hyperlocal. But NH voters have plenty else on their minds.
NH.summary: New Hampshire voters participated in March 10 town elections amid unseasonably warm weather, with many citing national and global issues like the war in Iran and rising oil costs alongside local municipal budgets and zoning decisions.

NJ.title: Candidates in NJ special House election trade charges of extremism
NJ.summary: Democrat Analilia Mejia and Republican Joe Hathaway are trading charges of extremism ahead of the April 16 special general election for New Jersey's 11th Congressional District seat vacated by Governor Mikie Sherrill.

NJ.title: 58 line up to run in congressional primaries as Democrats eye gains
NJ.summary: Fifty-eight candidates filed for New Jersey's congressional primaries by the March 23 deadline, with 39 Democrats and 19 Republicans vying for seats in the June 2 primary as Democrats target Republican-held districts.

NJ.title: New Jersey Primaries Set for June 2 After Filing Deadline
NJ.summary: With the candidate filing deadline passed, New Jersey's primary fields are set for the June 2 election, including competitive races in the 2nd, 7th, 8th, and 12th congressional districts.

NM.title: NM GOP selects two candidates for gubernatorial primary ballot at pre-primary convention
NM.summary: Republican delegates chose Rio Rancho Mayor Gregg Hull and former gubernatorial candidate Doug Turner to compete in the June 2 primary, while former PRC Commissioner James Ellison dropped out after failing to get enough delegate support.

NM.title: 19 NM House seats draw primary challenges
NM.summary: As the filing deadline closed on March 10, nineteen of New Mexico's 70 House seats drew contested primary elections for the June 2 primary, the first election to feature the state's new semi-open primary system.

NM.title: New Mexico Election 2026: trail notes
NM.summary: Roundup of campaign developments including former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland winning 74% of Democratic delegate votes for governor at the pre-primary convention and analysis of key primary matchups.

NM.title: New Mexico enacts law prohibiting the deployment of troops to polling places
NM.summary: Governor Lujan Grisham signed SB 264 on March 9, making New Mexico the first state to ban armed federal agents and military troops from polling places and ballot drop box locations, with state-level penalties for violations.

NM.title: New Mexico lawmakers approve three pieces of election-related legislation in 2026 session
NM.summary: The 2026 New Mexico legislative session produced three election-related measures: SB 264 (banning troops at polling places), HB 248 (requiring voter approval for capital bonds), and SJR 1 (removing outdated constitutional language on school elections).

NY.title: Internal GOP poll shows Blakeman just 9 points behind Hochul
NY.summary: An internal Republican poll shows Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman trailing Governor Hochul by just 9 points (52%-43%) in the governor's race, though independent polling shows a wider 20-point gap.

NC.title: After one of smoothest election days in recent history, post-election processes underway
NC.summary: North Carolina's March 3 primary drew more than 1.5 million voters (19.7% turnout, up 5% from 2022), with the State Board of Elections calling it 'one of the smoothest Election Days in recent history.'

NC.title: Berger-Page race likely to go to a recount, and other NC primary election results
NC.summary: The Republican primary for NC Senate District 26 headed to a recount with Sheriff Sam Page leading longtime Senate President Pro Tem Phil Berger by just 2 votes out of more than 26,000 cast.

NC.title: State Board releases number of provisional ballots cast by county, voting method in 2026 primary election
NC.summary: The NCSBE released provisional ballot data from the March 3 primary, including ballots cast by voters who did not present acceptable photo ID and completed Photo ID Exception Forms.

NC.title: State Board certifies state and local primary contests, to consider most federal contests in April
NC.summary: The NC State Board unanimously certified results for all state and local primary contests, deferring certification of U.S. Senate and several U.S. House races to an April meeting; Phil Berger conceded the District 26 recount to Sam Page.

NC.title: North Carolina elections board certifies 2026 primary results, excluding a few races
NC.summary: The certification included former Governor Roy Cooper and former RNC Chair Michael Whatley as Senate primary winners, setting up a marquee November general election matchup.

ND.title: SAVE Act contains exemption for North Dakota voters, but questions remain as Senate debate continues
ND.summary: The federal SAVE America Act includes an exemption for North Dakota as the only state without voter registration, but voting rights groups raise concerns it could still create barriers for tribal citizens whose IDs may not state citizenship.

ND.title: Protecting voter rights, democracy a theme of Fargo No Kings
ND.summary: A 'No Kings' rally in Fargo focused on protecting voter rights and democracy, with speakers expressing concerns about federal election legislation and its potential impact on North Dakota's unique no-registration voting system.

ND.title: Attendance down as North Dakota Republicans hold convention without statewide officials
ND.summary: The North Dakota Republican Party held its state convention in Minot with 707 delegates, about half the turnout from two years prior, as statewide elected officials were notably absent from the event.

OH.title: DeWine signs bill banning Ohio communities from using ranked choice voting
OH.summary: Governor DeWine signed Senate Bill 63, making Ohio the 19th state to ban ranked choice voting. The bipartisan bill prohibits Ohio communities from adopting the alternative voting method and withholds state funding from local governments that use it.

OH.title: Secretary of State LaRose issues seventh election security directive
OH.summary: Secretary of State Frank LaRose issued his seventh election security directive, providing each of Ohio's 88 county boards of elections a $10,000 security grant and requiring cybersecurity audits to be completed by August 31, 2026.

OH.title: SB 293 absentee ballot deadline changes take effect ahead of May primary
OH.summary: Ohio's SB 293 took effect March 20, eliminating the four-day post-Election Day grace period for absentee ballots. All mail-in ballots must now be received by 7:30 PM on Election Day. The law also directs more frequent citizenship verification using state and federal databases.

OK.title: Oklahoma AG settles with DOJ over voter registration data
OK.summary: Attorney General Gentner Drummond entered a settlement with the U.S. DOJ, agreeing to provide Oklahoma's complete statewide voter registration database -- including names, birth dates, addresses, and identifying numbers -- in exchange for dismissal of the federal lawsuit.

OK.title: Voting rights groups move to intervene in DOJ voter data lawsuit
OK.summary: The League of Women Voters of Oklahoma, LULAC, and a naturalized citizen, represented by the ACLU, filed a motion to intervene in the DOJ voter data case, seeking to block the release of private voter information including driver's license and Social Security data.

OK.title: Oklahoma candidate filing period opens April 1 for 2026 primary
OK.summary: The State Election Board announced the three-day candidate filing period running April 1-3 for the June 16 primary elections. The party registration change deadline of March 31 was also noted for voters wanting to participate in a different party's primary.

OR.title: US Supreme Court could end Oregon's practice of accepting ballots after Election Day
OR.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court heard arguments in a Mississippi case that could invalidate Oregon's 2022 law allowing ballots arriving up to a week after Election Day to be counted if postmarked on time. A ruling expected by June or July could affect Oregon and 13 other states with similar policies.

PA.title: What to know about Pennsylvania's 2026 special elections
PA.summary: Republicans held onto two state House seats in March 17 special elections: Andrea Verobish won District 79 with 56% of the vote and Catherine Wallen won District 193 with 59.7%, maintaining the party balance in the closely divided chamber.

PA.title: 21 states urge Supreme Court to uphold Pennsylvania mail ballot date requirement
PA.summary: Twenty-one state attorneys general filed an amicus brief urging the U.S. Supreme Court to reverse a federal appeals court decision that struck down Pennsylvania's requirement that voters handwrite the date on mail-in ballot envelopes, arguing the rule is a valid election safeguard.

RI.title: Rhode Island electronic voting bill for disabled and military voters advances to governor
RI.summary: Rhode Island's H7007, which makes permanent the electronic ballot portal for disabled, military, and overseas voters, was transmitted to the governor on March 26, 2026. The bill renews a pilot program that expired December 31, 2025, and passed the House 61-8.

SC.title: South Carolina opens 2026 candidate filing period for statewide primaries
SC.summary: South Carolina opened candidate filing on March 16 for the June 9 primaries. All seven U.S. House seats, one U.S. Senate seat, all statewide constitutional offices, and all 124 state House seats are on the ballot. Filing closes March 30.

SC.title: South Carolina candidates officially file for 2026 primary ballots
SC.summary: The two-week candidate filing period officially opened, with notable early filings including Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette, Attorney General Alan Wilson, and several congressional incumbents. The June 9 primary and potential June 23 runoff will set the field for November.

SD.title: Rhoden signs bill requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote
SD.summary: Governor Rhoden signed SB 175 (the South Dakota SAVE Act) with an emergency clause making it effective immediately. First-time voter registrants must now provide proof of U.S. citizenship for state elections; those who cannot may register as "federal voters" for presidential and congressional races only.

SD.title: South Dakota signs six election integrity bills into law
SD.summary: Governor Rhoden signed six election-related bills as emergencies, effective immediately before the June 2 primary. The bills address proof of citizenship for voter registration, campaign finance disclosures, election results publication, absentee ballot processing, voter registration file publication, and nomination petition submission.

SD.title: South Dakota Secretary of State issues guidance on new voter registration law
SD.summary: Secretary of State Monae Johnson released guidance on SB 175, clarifying that current registered voters are unaffected. Acceptable citizenship documents include a SD driver's license issued after July 1, 2025, tribal ID card, or a copy of a passport or birth certificate.

TN.title: Tennessee joins 20 states urging SCOTUS to uphold Pennsylvania mail ballot date requirement
TN.summary: Tennessee Attorney General Jonathan Skrmetti joined 20 other state attorneys general in filing an amicus brief urging the U.S. Supreme Court to uphold Pennsylvania's requirement that voters handwrite the date on mail-in ballot envelopes, calling it a reasonable election safeguard.

TN.title: SAVE Act and pending state legislation could impact voting in Tennessee
TN.summary: Tennessee elections officials are preparing for potential federal and state election law changes ahead of the 2026 election season. The federal SAVE Act would add citizenship verification requirements, though Tennessee's existing strict ID laws mean relatively modest impact.

TN.title: Landmark voting reform clears financial barriers for formerly incarcerated in Tennessee
TN.summary: Senate Bill 336 and House Bill 687, sponsored by Sen. Akbari and Rep. Camper, passed both chambers and head to the governor's desk. The bills remove the requirement to pay all outstanding court costs before voting rights restoration and allow those compliant with child support payment plans for 12 months to restore rights.

TX.title: Five Takeaways From the March 2026 Texas Primaries
TX.summary: Analysis of the March 3 primary results including the Cornyn-Paxton Senate runoff, Talarico's Democratic Senate win, record-high turnout of 22.1% among 18.6 million registered voters, and multiple down-ballot upsets.

TX.title: Texas Primary Election Results: How Texas Politics Impacts Your Market
TX.summary: Analysis of the March 3 Texas primary results, with Cornyn and Paxton heading to a May 26 runoff in the most expensive Senate primary on record at over $122 million in ad spending.

UT.title: 2026 Utah Legislature Ends With Feelings of One Long 'Groundhog Day'
UT.summary: The 2026 Utah legislative session ended after passing 541 of 1,015 filed bills, including election-related measures SB 194 requiring signature and ID verification on ballots and HB 209 requiring proof of citizenship for state voter registration.

UT.title: 2026 Elections: Utah's New Court-Ordered Map Draws 41 Candidates for Congress
UT.summary: Utah's court-ordered congressional redistricting map has drawn 41 candidates for four House seats, with one district leaning heavily Democratic for the first time in decades.

UT.title: 2026 Election: Utah Democrats See 'Record-Breaking' Caucus Turnout With New Maps
UT.summary: Utah Democrats reported record-breaking caucus turnout on March 17, energized by the court-ordered congressional map that creates one heavily Democratic-leaning district.

UT.title: The 'Fascinating' Dynamics in Play for Utah's 2026 Congressional Primaries
UT.summary: Analysis of the dynamics shaping Utah's 2026 congressional primaries under the new court-ordered map, with Rep. Burgess Owens declining to seek reelection and competitive races developing across all four districts.

UT.title: Utah Redistricting Initiative to Repeal Proposition 4 Will Not Be on the 2026 Ballot
UT.summary: The effort to repeal Proposition 4 and eliminate Utah's independent redistricting commission will not appear on the 2026 ballot after enough voters withdrew their signatures to drop below the required threshold.

VT.title: Community Media Powers Vermont Civic Life on Town Meeting Day 2026
VT.summary: Coverage of how community media outlets across Vermont helped inform voters and cover local issues during the 2026 Town Meeting Day elections on March 3.

VA.title: Federal Judge Upholds Ruling That Certain Ex-Felons Should Not Automatically Lose Voting Rights
VA.summary: A federal court reaffirmed a January ruling that Virginia's blanket disenfranchisement of people with felony convictions violates post-Civil War Readmission Act requirements, limiting which felonies can trigger voting rights loss effective May 1, 2026.

VA.title: Four Weeks Before April 21 Referendum, Early Voting Shows Stronger Turnout in GOP-Leaning Areas
VA.summary: Early voting data for Virginia's April 21 redistricting referendum shows Republican-leaning congressional districts leading in turnout, with roughly 499,000 early votes cast as of late March, surpassing the same period in the 2025 gubernatorial election.

VA.title: Gov. Spanberger signs executive order aimed at protecting election integrity, rejoins ERIC
VA.summary: Governor Spanberger signed an executive order strengthening election security procedures and reentering Virginia into the 26-state Electronic Registration Information Center (ERIC), reversing former Governor Youngkin's 2023 withdrawal.

VA.title: Voting Rights Advocates Hail Virginia's Return to Multistate Voter Roll System
VA.summary: Voting rights groups praised Governor Spanberger's decision to rejoin ERIC, the multistate voter registration data-sharing system that helps identify duplicate registrations, voters who have moved, and deceased voters.

VA.title: Nearly 500,000 Have Voted Early in Virginia's Redistricting Referendum
