TX.title: Texas Standard for April 6, 2026: What Trump's election executive order could mean for voting
TX.summary: Reporting on the Trump executive order seeking to reshape election administration, including potential Postal Service involvement.

UT.title: Florida, South Dakota, Utah enact proof of citizenship laws for voter registration
UT.summary: Utah Gov. Spencer Cox signed HB 209 on March 25, 2026; the law takes effect May 6, 2026 and requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register.

UT.title: Utah enacts proof-of-citizenship bill, 13 other election-related bills during 2026 session
UT.summary: Recap of Utah's 2026 legislative session, which passed 14 election-related bills including HB 209 and SB 153.

UT.title: What to know about Utah's new voter privacy law and how clerks are responding to concerns
UT.summary: Explains SB 153, which takes effect April 6, 2026 and makes previously-private voter records public unless voters apply for at-risk status.

UT.title: Utah makes voter rolls more transparent as Trump DOJ sues state
UT.summary: Utah's SB 153 broadens public access to voter rolls just as the DOJ presses its suit against Utah (one of 29 states) seeking full voter registration lists.

UT.title: Some Utah voters weigh unregistering because of new law lifting certain privacy protections
UT.summary: Some Utahns are considering deregistering in response to SB 153 exposing their personal information.

VT.title: A 14-year-old running for governor is the first teen to get on Vermont's general election ballot
VT.summary: Dean Roy, a 14-year-old Stowe High School freshman, qualified for the Vermont general election ballot for governor — a first in the state.

VT.title: Union, Secretary of State launch high school senior voter registration drive
VT.summary: Vermont Secretary of State Sarah Copeland Hanzas and Vermont-NEA launched 'Vermont State Champions for Democracy,' a high school voter registration contest.

VA.title: Virginia joins a national effort to ensure only popular vote winners become president
VA.summary: Gov. Abigail Spanberger signed legislation making Virginia the 18th jurisdiction to join the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact.

VA.title: Amending Virginia: Pro- and anti-redistricting camps wield 'fairness' in voter appeals
VA.summary: Coverage of the competing campaigns around the April 21 constitutional amendment referendum, which would allow the General Assembly to temporarily redraw congressional districts.

VA.title: Decision Virginia: What's on your ballot on April 21?
VA.summary: Guide to the April 21 special election, where Virginia voters will decide a single statewide constitutional amendment.

WA.title: Months later, DOJ lawsuit to obtain WA voter rolls can move forward
WA.summary: A federal judge ruled the Trump administration's December 2025 lawsuit against Washington over its voter rolls can proceed after months of service delays.

WA.title: State GOP looking to change voting laws, secretary of state calls fraud 'incredibly rare'
WA.summary: The Washington State GOP is gathering signatures for IP26-500, a ballot initiative that would require one-time proof of citizenship to register to vote.

WA.title: Federal attacks on vote-by-mail, voter eligibility worry WA election officials
WA.summary: Washington county auditors and election officials report concern over Trump administration executive orders targeting mail voting.

WV.title: U.S. DOJ moves to compel West Virginia to release unredacted voter info, asserting broad investigative power
WV.summary: The DOJ filed a motion to compel West Virginia Secretary of State Kris Warner to release unredacted voter registration records.

WV.title: W.Va. Citizens Action Group files motion against DOJ effort to obtain voter records
WV.summary: The West Virginia Citizens Action Group filed a motion to intervene as defendant in the DOJ's lawsuit seeking voter registration records.

WV.title: New ID rules, closed GOP primary: What to know for West Virginia's May 12 election
WV.summary: Explains the new photo-ID-only requirement (HB 3016), the newly closed Republican primary, the April 21 registration deadline, and early voting April 29-May 9.

WV.title: Election 2026: Voter registration deadline is April 21; what you need to know to vote
WV.summary: Coverage of the April 21 voter registration deadline for West Virginia's May 12 primary.

WV.title: West Virginia announces new voter ID and deadline rules for 2026 primaries
WV.summary: Rundown of the voting changes West Virginians will see in the May 12 primary, including mandatory photo ID at the polls and the state's new closed Republican primary rules.

WI.title: Wisconsin updates election certification law; Evers vetoes HAVA complaint bill
WI.summary: Gov. Tony Evers signed a bill aligning Wisconsin's presidential election certification deadlines with the federal Electoral Count Reform Act.

WI.title: Liberals gain seat on Wisconsin Supreme Court, adding to firewall in voting cases
WI.summary: Chris Taylor won the April 1 Wisconsin Supreme Court election by roughly 20 points, expanding the court's liberal majority from 4-3 to 5-2.

WI.title: Taylor wins the 2026 Wisconsin Supreme Court election
WI.summary: Chris Taylor defeated her opponent in the Wisconsin Supreme Court race, securing a 10-year term and strengthening liberal control.

WI.title: Absentee Ballot Report - April 7, 2026 Spring Election
WI.summary: The Wisconsin Elections Commission released its absentee-ballot data for the April 7, 2026 spring election.

WY.title: Gray defends decision to share sensitive Wyoming voter data with feds as voter group, Dems criticize move
WY.summary: Secretary of State Chuck Gray defended his decision to share personally-identifiable voter data (including dates of birth and partial SSNs) with the U.S. Department of Justice.

WY.title: Wyoming lawyer files complaint against Gray for providing voter data to feds
WY.summary: A Cheyenne attorney filed a complaint with the Wyoming Attorney General alleging Secretary of State Chuck Gray violated state law.

WY.title: What Natrona County voters need to know for this year's upcoming elections
WY.summary: Natrona County election officials outline 2026 changes including the new HB 156 requirements for physical proof of residency and U.S. citizenship at registration.

WY.title: Attorney says Chuck Gray lost privacy on voter info by texting news outlet
WY.summary: A lawyer argues that because Secretary Gray texted a news outlet about his release of confidential voter data to the DOJ, he waived any claim of privacy.

WY.title: Secretary of State Gray continues voter list maintenance efforts
WY.summary: Gray's office referred an additional 514 voter records to Wyoming county clerks for possible removal from voter rolls.

AL.title: Alabama and Tennessee join rush of southern states moving to redraw maps after Supreme Court ruling
AL.summary: Alabama joined a wave of southern states moving to redraw congressional maps after the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling weakened Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, with Gov. Kay Ivey calling a special legislative session.

AL.title: Gov. Kay Ivey calls special legislative session as Alabama seeks legal permission to redistrict
AL.summary: Gov. Ivey called a special session as Alabama asked the U.S. Supreme Court to lift an injunction that blocked the state's 2023 GOP-drawn congressional map, potentially affecting the state's primary elections.

AL.title: Alabama Legislature to begin special session with redistricting possible
AL.summary: Alabama lawmakers convened a special session to consider legislation enabling a replacement primary in affected districts if a federal court lifts the injunction on the state's 2023 congressional map.

AL.title: Chaos: Alabama prepares to eliminate majority-Black districts, while moving forward with elections it may annul
AL.summary: Reports on Alabama's contingency plan to call a replacement primary if courts permit a new congressional map, while the state proceeds with its scheduled May 19 primary election.

AL.title: Alabama special session kicks off as state leaders await redistricting court decisions
AL.summary: Alabama's special session opened as legislators prepared contingency election legislation while awaiting U.S. Supreme Court and Eleventh Circuit decisions on the state's congressional maps.

AK.title: Public hearing planned for voter initiatives in Alaska
AK.summary: The Alaska Legislature scheduled a public hearing on three ballot initiatives certified for the November ballot, including a ranked-choice voting repeal, campaign contribution limit changes, and a citizen voting affirmation.

AK.title: Gov. Dunleavy vetoes election reform bill, citing concerns over timeline ahead of 2026 election
AK.summary: Gov. Mike Dunleavy vetoed SB 64, a bipartisan elections bill that would have created a ballot tracking and curing system, postage-paid return envelopes, and other reforms, citing implementation timeline concerns.

AK.title: Veto override vote on elections bill fails as two Southeast Alaska lawmakers flip
AK.summary: An attempt to override Gov. Dunleavy's veto of the election reform bill failed by two votes after Sen. Bert Stedman and Rep. Jeremy Bynum withdrew their support.

AK.title: Alaska lawmakers fall 2 votes short of overriding Dunleavy's veto of election bill
AK.summary: The Alaska Legislature voted 38-22 to sustain Gov. Dunleavy's veto, falling two short of the 40 votes needed to override and enact ballot tracking, ballot curing, and rural-liaison provisions.

AZ.title: Judge dismisses Justice Department lawsuit over Arizona's voter rolls
AZ.summary: U.S. District Judge Susan Brnovich dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit seeking unredacted Arizona voter roll data, including Social Security numbers and full birthdates, ruling federal law does not require such disclosure.

AZ.title: The Supreme Court weakened the Voting Rights Act. It may change how maps are drawn in Arizona.
AZ.summary: The Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais decision narrowing Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act could affect how Arizona's Independent Redistricting Commission draws maps, with potential near-term challenges to existing districts.

AR.title: Voting Rights Act ruling could have major impact in Arkansas, groups say
AR.summary: Civil rights advocates including the Arkansas NAACP warned the U.S. Supreme Court's 6-3 decision weakening Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act could threaten minority representation in Arkansas, where Republican-majority bodies control map-drawing.

CA.title: L.A. County Begins Mailing Vote by Mail Ballots for the 2026 Statewide Direct Primary Election
CA.summary: Los Angeles County began mailing vote-by-mail ballots to all registered voters for the June 2 statewide direct primary election, ahead of the statewide May 4 mailing deadline.

CA.title: California Voting Rights Act of 2026 Approved by Senate Committees
CA.summary: SB 1164 and SB 1360 (the California Voting Rights Act of 2026) were approved by the Senate Elections and Constitutional Amendments Committee, and SB 1164 also cleared the Senate Judiciary Committee, advancing landmark expansions to state voting protections.

CA.title: Supreme Court ruling on voting won't change California districts, but could hurt Democrats
CA.summary: Reports on how the U.S. Supreme Court's narrowing of the Voting Rights Act will not alter California's existing congressional map but may affect Latino representation and challenge local maps drawn under Section 2.

CO.title: Colorado likely shielded from major effects of Supreme Court's voting rights ruling
CO.summary: Colorado's independent redistricting commissions and the 2025 Colorado Voting Rights Act are expected to insulate the state from the worst impacts of the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais decision narrowing Section 2.

CO.title: Group tied to Democratic leadership in US House is funding attempt to redraw Colorado's congressional map
CO.summary: House Majority Forward, a nonprofit tied to House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, gave $150,000 to Coloradans For a Level Playing Field, an issue committee seeking to put a midcycle redistricting measure on the November 2026 ballot.

CO.title: Redistricting is rampant ahead of the US House midterm elections. What states are taking action?
CO.summary: Roundup news report on midcycle redistricting efforts across states including Colorado, where a proposed ballot measure would temporarily redraw the state's congressional map for the 2028 and 2030 elections.

CT.title: What CT voting registrars are saying about SAVE Act
CT.summary: Connecticut registrars and Secretary of State Stephanie Thomas reported widespread voter confusion - especially among married women - about the federal SAVE Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register.

CT.title: CT House postpones vote on universal absentee voting
CT.summary: A protracted debate in the Connecticut House on HB 5001, the universal no-excuse absentee voting bill, ended without a vote after Republicans extended floor debate over a rejected amendment.

DE.title: Governor Meyer Establishes Election Security Task Force in Delaware
DE.summary: Gov. Matt Meyer signed Executive Order 19 establishing the Delaware Task Force on Free, Fair, and Secure Elections. The 20-member panel, co-chaired by the Secretary of State and Secretary of Safety and Homeland Security, will assess threats including cybersecurity, voter intimidation, and disinformation.

DE.title: Meyer creates task force on election security: 'we must be proactive'
DE.summary: Coverage of Gov. Meyer's executive order launching an election security task force, framed as a proactive measure to safeguard Delaware elections from federal interference and other threats heading into the 2026 cycle.

DE.title: Delaware creates task force to Trump-proof its elections
DE.summary: Reports on Delaware's new task force, framing it as an effort to insulate state elections from Trump administration directives, including the federal voter eligibility executive order being challenged in court.

FL.title: Florida election law challenged in court over new ID requirements
FL.summary: Reports on additional legal challenges to HB 991, including a lawsuit by the Florida State Conference of the NAACP and the Florida Alliance for Retired Americans filed in Tallahassee federal court targeting the law's documentary proof of citizenship requirements.

FL.title: Civil Rights Groups Sue over Florida's New Election Law
FL.summary: Civil rights organizations filed additional federal challenges to HB 991, arguing the citizenship verification regime tied to DHSMV records would disenfranchise eligible voters and violate the First and 14th Amendments.

GA.title: First Day of Early Voting Sees Record Turnout
GA.summary: Georgia's first day of early voting for the May 19 primary saw 35,352 in-person ballots cast, a 29% increase over the 2022 primary and a record for a midterm primary.

GA.title: Kemp won't order redistricting in Georgia after Supreme Court weakens Voting Rights Act
GA.summary: Gov. Brian Kemp announced Georgia will not redraw its congressional maps for the 2026 elections following the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling, citing that early voting is already underway. Kemp said new maps will be adopted before the 2028 cycle.

GA.title: As Georgians Head to the Polls for Second Week of Early Voting, Record Breaking Turnout Continues
GA.summary: Over 214,000 Georgians cast ballots in the first 7 days of early voting for the May 19 primary, a 28% increase over the same period in 2022, continuing the record-setting pace.

GA.title: More than 250K early votes cast as Georgia continues breaking records
GA.summary: More than 250,000 early and absentee votes have been cast ahead of Georgia's May 19, 2026 primary; an Emory University political scientist projected total primary turnout could approach 2 million.

GA.title: Supreme Court decision weakening Voting Rights Act could impact future political maps in Georgia
GA.summary: Coverage of how the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling narrowing Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act may reshape future redistricting fights in Georgia and the South.

ID.title: Early 2026 primary election voting begins today in Canyon, other Idaho counties
ID.summary: Early voting for Idaho's May 19 primary opened in Bannock, Canyon, Twin Falls, Blaine and several other counties on April 27, with additional counties beginning the following week through May 15.

ID.title: Idaho amends voter ID affidavit process, enacts 14 other election bills in 2026
ID.summary: Recap of 15 election bills signed by Gov. Brad Little in the 2026 session, including S 1322, which now requires voters using the affidavit alternative to photo ID to also provide their date of birth or driver's license/ID number.

ID.title: Jerome County early voting underway with new location
ID.summary: Jerome County's early voting for the May 19 primary is underway at a new location; officials project 25-35% turnout, with activity expected to pick up as election day approaches.

IL.title: House approves redistricting amendment, fearing federal Voting Rights Act will be eliminated
IL.summary: The Illinois House voted 74-38 to advance a constitutional amendment establishing rules for legislative map drawing aimed at preserving minority representation, in anticipation of a U.S. Supreme Court ruling weakening the federal Voting Rights Act.

IL.title: Illinois lawmakers punt remap amendment after SCOTUS Voting Rights Act ruling
IL.summary: Senate President Don Harmon said the Illinois Senate will not advance the redistricting constitutional amendment following the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling that struck down a majority-Black district and narrowed Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act.

IN.title: Indiana college ID voting ban goes back into effect as injunction is stayed
IN.summary: A 7th Circuit panel granted an emergency stay of the preliminary injunction against SEA 10, restoring Indiana's ban on using student IDs at the polls just days after a federal district court had blocked it.

IN.title: COLLEGE ID BAN RETURNS: 7th Circuit lets Indiana prohibit use of student identification at polls
IN.summary: Coverage of the 7th Circuit's stay of the preliminary injunction against SEA 10, with the appeals court ruling that voting rules should not be altered so close to the May 6 primary; litigation continues in district court.

IN.title: Appeals court allows enforcement of Indiana law banning student ID for voting
IN.summary: Ballotpedia summary of the 7th Circuit's order staying Judge Richard Young's preliminary injunction, allowing Indiana to enforce SEA 10's prohibition on student IDs at the polls during the 2026 primary.

IN.title: Appeals Court reinstates Student ID Voting Ban amid ongoing Indiana primaries
IN.summary: Reports that the 7th Circuit reinstated Indiana's student ID ban while early voting was already underway for the May 6 primary, with state officials saying only government-issued IDs will be accepted at the polls.

IN.title: Live blog: Indiana's 2026 primary election
IN.summary: Live coverage of Indiana's May 5 statewide primary, with reports of doubled early-voting turnout in Marion County and high early turnout in Hamilton County compared to recent primaries.

IA.title: Secretary of State shares Iowa voting records with the DOJ
IA.summary: Iowa Secretary of State Paul Pate confirmed his office turned over Iowa voter registration records, including driver's license numbers and partial Social Security numbers, to the U.S. Department of Justice after consulting with the state Attorney General's office about federal compliance obligations.

IA.title: Iowa shares sensitive voter data with the Department of Justice
IA.summary: Iowa joined other states in providing voter registration data to the DOJ under the Civil Rights Act of 1960. Pate said the state will follow the National Voter Registration Act when handling any voter eligibility issues flagged by federal officials.

IA.title: Gov. Reynolds signs list of bills into law on May 3rd
IA.summary: Governor Reynolds signed HF 2501, an act relating to the conduct of elections, into law on May 3, 2026 as part of the close of the 2026 legislative session.

IA.title: Lawmakers pass final budgets, property tax bill and more at end of 2026 session
IA.summary: The Iowa legislature adjourned its 2026 session, having passed a constitutional amendment to require a two-thirds supermajority for any future state income tax rate increases that will go to voters in November.

IA.title: Iowa GOP aims to pass SAVE Act
IA.summary: Reports on Iowa Senate File 2203, which would require the Secretary of State to verify each registered voter's citizenship status using the federal SAVE database, with potential cancellation of registration after 90 days for unconfirmed voters.

KS.title: Kansas legislators override veto on citizenship checks for voter list maintenance, enact three other election bills in 2026 session
KS.summary: Recap of the Kansas legislature's 2026 session, including the override of Gov. Kelly's veto of the SAVE Kansas Act, which directs the Secretary of State to cross-check voter rolls against the federal SAVE database, taking effect July 1.

KS.title: Kansas Lawmakers end legislative session with attack on voters, immigrants, and due process for all
KS.summary: ACLU of Kansas summarizes 2026 session voting-related legislation enacted, including the SAVE Kansas Act enabling broader voter roll purges through cross-agency data sharing.

KY.title: Kentucky legislators override four vetoes on election-related bills
KY.summary: Summary of Kentucky General Assembly's veto overrides on four election bills, including HB 139 (omnibus elections bill restricting voter ID forms, expanding voter list maintenance, and barring barcodes/QR codes for vote tabulation).

LA.title: U.S. House primaries in Louisiana are suspended after Voting Rights Act ruling
LA.summary: Gov. Jeff Landry issued an executive order suspending Louisiana's May 16 U.S. House primary contests after the Supreme Court's April 29 ruling in Louisiana v. Callais struck down the state's congressional map; other races on the May 16 ballot will continue.

LA.title: Louisiana governor postpones U.S. House primary elections after Supreme Court ruling
LA.summary: Coverage of Gov. Landry's executive order delaying U.S. House primaries until July 15 or as determined by the Legislature, while Sec. of State Nancy Landry stated House races will remain on ballots but votes will not be counted.

LA.title: Early voting begins for May 16 election in La.
LA.summary: Early voting opened May 2 across Louisiana for the May 16 election; voters may still see U.S. House races on ballots though those votes will not be counted under the suspension order.

LA.title: Court agrees to immediately finalize Voting Rights Act decision
LA.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court granted a request to immediately finalize its Louisiana v. Callais opinion, bypassing the standard 32-day waiting period to allow Louisiana to redraw its congressional map for the 2026 elections.

LA.title: Louisiana election delay sparks flurry of court action
LA.summary: Lawsuits in state and federal court challenge Gov. Landry's suspension of the U.S. House primaries; voters who already cast ballots and a candidate (Rep. Cleo Fields) argue the election was already underway and must continue.

ME.title: Maine Joins Lawsuit Against Trump Administration Over Pres. Trump's Election Integrity Executive Order
ME.summary: Maine joined a multi-state lawsuit challenging the Trump administration's election integrity executive order, with Sec. of State Shenna Bellows arguing it unconstitutionally usurps states' authority to run federal elections.

MD.title: Gov. Wes Moore signs voting rights, immigration, foster care bills
MD.summary: Gov. Moore signed the Maryland Voting Rights Act of 2026 into law as part of a 197-bill signing ceremony; the emergency law took effect immediately and creates a state-level voting rights regime applicable to county and municipal elections.

MD.title: Maryland Democrats hope brand-new state Voting Rights Act holds in face of Supreme Court ruling
MD.summary: Maryland Democrats reacted to the Maryland Voting Rights Act taking effect just one day before the U.S. Supreme Court's April 29 Louisiana v. Callais ruling weakened federal Voting Rights Act protections in redistricting.

MD.title: Championed by Del. Wims, Gov. Moore signs Voting Rights Act
MD.summary: Coverage of the bill signing ceremony with House Speaker Pena-Melnyk and bill sponsors, focused on the new state law's protections against voting discrimination at the local and municipal level.

MD.title: Maryland Voting Rights Act Bill Prohibiting Discrimination in Voting Signed into Law
MD.summary: NAACP LDF announcement on the Maryland Voting Rights Act being signed, providing the state Attorney General authority to address discrimination in local and municipal voting practices.

MA.title: What To Know Ahead Of Brookline's 2026 Town Election
MA.summary: Local Massachusetts election preview covering Brookline's May 5 town election, including registration, early voting deadlines, and a $23.2M tax override question.

MI.title: Garlin Gilchrist wins Democratic nomination for secretary of state
MI.summary: Michigan Lt. Gov. Garlin Gilchrist II won the Democratic nomination for secretary of state at the state party's endorsement convention on April 19, 2026, setting up a competitive general election against Republican Macomb County Clerk Anthony Forlini.

MI.title: Trump administration demands 2024 election ballots from Wayne County, Michigan
MI.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice sent a demand letter to Wayne County Clerk Cathy Garrett seeking more than 860,000 ballots, envelopes, and receipts from the 2024 general election, threatening a court order if records are not turned over within 14 days.

MI.title: AG Nessel, Governor Whitmer, Secretary Benson Denounce DOJ Demand for 2024 Ballots
MI.summary: Top Michigan Democratic officials denounced the DOJ's demand for Wayne County 2024 ballots as 'absurd' and pledged to fight any federal court action, calling the request based on discredited fraud claims.

MI.title: Antrim County voters confused after clerk attempts to cancel hundreds of voter registrations
MI.summary: Hundreds of Antrim County voters are reportedly affected after Clerk Victoria Bishop attempted to cancel voter registrations; the Michigan Bureau of Elections said the actions fell outside her authority and failed to comply with the law.

MI.title: Secretary Benson announces over 2.1 million outdated voter registrations canceled or identified for cancellation since 2019
MI.summary: Secretary Benson announced more than 2.1 million outdated voter registrations have been canceled or identified for cancellation since 2019, framing the maintenance as careful list cleanup compliant with the law.

MN.title: What's actually in the SAVE Act — an interactive explainer
MN.summary: An interactive explainer outlining the federal SAVE Act's requirements that voters prove citizenship — typically with a birth certificate or passport — to register, with discussion of how it would affect Minnesota voters.

MN.title: Senate Passes Elections Policy Bill
MN.summary: The Minnesota Senate passed SF 4223, the Elections Policy Bill, which raises penalties for voter and election-official intimidation from a gross misdemeanor to a felony, increases maximum civil penalties to $10,000, and tightens presidential candidate eligibility checks.

MN.title: Walz delivers final State of the State address, commending Minnesotans' compassion during tragedy
MN.summary: Gov. Tim Walz delivered his final State of the State address on April 28, 2026, framing his term ahead of the 2026 election cycle in which he is not seeking reelection.

MS.title: Letter to Secretary of State Urging Compliance with the National Voter Registration Act Following Signage of SHIELD Act
MS.summary: A coalition including the ACLU of Mississippi, League of Women Voters of Mississippi, Mississippi Votes, and Disability Rights Mississippi sent an NVRA notice letter to Secretary of State Michael Watson on April 10, 2026, alerting officials that the SHIELD Act may violate the National Voter Registration Act and signaling potential litigation.

MS.title: Letter to MS Secretary of State Raises Concerns How the New SHIELD Act Violates the National Voter Registration Act
MS.summary: Companion announcement of the April 10 NVRA notice letter sent to Secretary Watson, detailing how the SHIELD Act's documentary proof-of-citizenship triggers and timeline could disenfranchise eligible voters in violation of federal law.

MS.title: US Supreme Court Callais decision just weakened the Voting Rights Act. What happens next in Mississippi?
MS.summary: Reports on how the U.S. Supreme Court's Callais ruling weakening Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act will affect pending and future Mississippi redistricting and voting-rights cases.

MO.title: Supreme Court voting rights decision could affect Missouri's 1st Congressional District
MO.summary: Analysis of how the U.S. Supreme Court's recent Voting Rights Act decision could reshape Missouri's 1st Congressional District and future redistricting battles.

MO.title: Missouri ballot questions take opposite approaches to voter-passed policies
MO.summary: Coverage of Respect Missouri Voters delivering more than 367,000 signatures to put a constitutional amendment on the ballot that would protect voter-initiated laws from legislative repeal, contrasted with the GOP-backed Amendment 4 already on the 2026 ballot.

MT.title: 3 ways Montana Free Press' 2026 Election Guide can help you cast your ballot
MT.summary: Montana Free Press launched its nonpartisan 2026 Election Guide ahead of the June 2 primary, summarizing new rules including SB 276's photo-ID requirement, SB 490's noon Election-Day registration cutoff, and HB 719's mail-ballot birth-year requirement.

MT.title: School, special district election ballots due Tuesday
MT.summary: Reminder coverage of the May 5 deadline for Montana's school and special-district mail-ballot election, the first statewide test of the new mail-ballot signature and birth-year verification rules.

NE.title: Bill strengthening ban on foreign contributions to ballot question committees signed by Governor
NE.summary: Gov. Jim Pillen signed LB 1075 on April 15, 2026, expanding Nebraska's ban on foreign contributions to ballot-measure committees, requiring committees to certify they have not received foreign-national funds, and increasing fines for violations to $100,000 or the prohibited amount.

NE.title: Pillen renews attack on Nebraska ballot initiative process
NE.summary: At the LB 1075 signing ceremony, Gov. Pillen renewed criticism of Nebraska's ballot-initiative process, calling for additional restrictions beyond the new foreign-funding ban.

NE.title: Nebraska legislative session ends for 2026; lawmakers sustain five vetoes
NE.summary: The Nebraska Legislature adjourned its 2026 session on April 17 after enacting five election-related bills (LB 1075, LB 784, LB 798, LB 986, LB 1135) and sustaining five Pillen vetoes.

NE.title: Nebraska becomes second state to enact or expand a foreign funding ban for ballot measures this year
NE.summary: Ballotpedia analysis placing Nebraska's LB 1075 in national context as the second state in 2026 to enact or expand a foreign-funding ban targeting ballot-measure campaigns.

NE.title: Nebraska expands foreign funding ban for ballot measures, enacts four other election laws in 2026 session
NE.summary: End-of-session recap detailing all five election laws enacted: LB 1075 (foreign-funding ban), LB 784 (sheriff residency), LB 798 (ward elections in second-class cities), LB 986 (campaign funds for security), and LB 1135 (voter approval for water-system transfers to tribes).

NV.title: Trump Initiatives May Disrupt Nevada Election
NV.summary: Reports that Nevada Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar is coordinating with county clerks and sheriffs on contingency plans to respond if Trump's executive order to create a national voter list and restrict USPS mail-ballot delivery takes effect.

NV.title: Number of registered voters in Nevada up by nearly 21,000 in April
NV.summary: Nevada added 20,805 active registered voters in April 2026 (a 1.02% increase) bringing the active total to 2,061,557; nonpartisans accounted for 11,467 of the new registrations.

NH.title: With student IDs banned at the polls, NH issues new guidance for college voters
NH.summary: After Gov. Ayotte signed HB 323 banning student IDs for voting, the NH Secretary of State issued new guidance for college students explaining acceptable government-issued IDs needed to cast ballots in upcoming elections.

NH.title: NH students must show valid ID, not student card, to vote
NH.summary: Coverage explaining that as of June 2, student IDs will no longer be accepted at NH polls and outlining what documentation students must obtain to remain eligible to vote.

NJ.title: New Jersey Election Chief Confident Despite Federal Pressure
NJ.summary: New Jersey's top election official expresses confidence in administering the upcoming June primary despite ongoing federal pressure and the Trump administration's executive order and lawsuit over voter rolls.

NM.title: New Mexico Continues to Rank Among Top 10 States for Election Administration
NM.summary: Secretary of State Maggie Toulouse Oliver announced New Mexico continues to rank among the top 10 states nationally for election administration based on a recent national assessment.

NM.title: New Mexico Primary 2026: Secretary of State
NM.summary: Profiles the two Democratic candidates competing for New Mexico Secretary of State in the June 2 primary — Santa Fe County Clerk Katharine Clark and Doña Ana County Clerk Amanda López Askin — as Maggie Toulouse Oliver is term-limited.

NM.title: New Mexico Democratic secretary of state candidates weigh in on gutting of Voting Rights Act
NM.summary: At a candidate forum, both Democratic Secretary of State candidates expressed grave concerns over the U.S. Supreme Court's recent decision narrowing Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act and discussed implications for New Mexico voters.

NM.title: As early voting opens, here's who is on the ballot and where to vote
NM.summary: Coverage of the start of in-person early voting at county clerk offices on May 5 for the New Mexico June 2 primary, with details on candidates, deadlines, and voting locations.

NY.title: Top Democrat aims for New York redistricting after Supreme Court's Voting Rights ruling
NY.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is deploying Rep. Joe Morelle to meet with Gov. Kathy Hochul and state legislators about mid-decade congressional redistricting in New York after the Supreme Court's recent ruling weakening Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act.

NC.title: State Board Identifies Deceased Individuals on Voter Rolls Through Federal Database Comparison
NC.summary: The NC State Board of Elections announced that comparison of 7.4 million voter records against the federal SAVE database (submitted April 17) flagged approximately 34,000 deceased individuals on the state's voter rolls; due-process procedures will be followed before any removals.

NC.title: North Carolina finds 34,000 deceased voters on rolls
NC.summary: WECT reports that the NC State Board's first SAVE database cross-check identified about 34,000 deceased people remaining on North Carolina's voter rolls.

NC.title: North Carolina identifies 34,000 deceased individuals on voter rolls
NC.summary: Coverage of NCSBE's announcement that the SAVE database initiative identified roughly 34,000 deceased voters; State Board says the find does not indicate fraudulent voting but underscores the need for regular roll maintenance.

NC.title: North Carolina finds 34,000 deceased voters on rolls
NC.summary: Local Chatham County coverage of the SAVE database comparison results identifying tens of thousands of deceased registrants on NC voter rolls.

OH.title: Election Day 2026: Ohioans vote in high-profile governor and Senate races
OH.summary: Coverage of Ohio's May 5 primary election with high-profile gubernatorial and U.S. Senate primaries, including former Sen. Sherrod Brown's Democratic Senate bid and Vivek Ramaswamy's GOP gubernatorial campaign.

OH.title: Ohio primary preview: four Republicans fighting to run for state Supreme Court
OH.summary: Preview of the four-way Republican primary for an Ohio Supreme Court seat ahead of the May 5 primary election.

OH.title: Primary elections in Ohio, Indiana offer latest temperature check on Trump popularity
OH.summary: NPR coverage of how Ohio's May 5 primary serves as an early gauge of GOP voter sentiment in the 2026 midterm cycle, with attention on the Senate and gubernatorial primaries.

OK.title: Oklahoma voters to decide constitutional amendment changing Judicial Nominating Commission structure on Nov. 3, 2026
OK.summary: Oklahoma voters will decide a constitutional amendment in November 2026 restructuring the state's Judicial Nominating Commission, including changes to appointment procedures, term lengths, and member eligibility.

OR.title: Ballots will start arriving soon ahead of Oregon primary
OR.summary: Ballots for Oregon's May 19 primary began mailing on April 29, 2026. All 3+ million registered voters will receive a ballot because of statewide Measure 120, though about 1.3 million unaffiliated voters cannot participate in partisan races until the general election.

OR.title: How hikes to Oregon gas taxes and fees ended up on the ballot
OR.summary: Oregon's May primary ballot includes Measure 120, asking voters whether to approve transportation funding increases via gas taxes and fees. The article describes the legislative path that led to the referral.

OR.title: USPS has begun delivering ballots for the upcoming May 19, 2026 Primary Election
OR.summary: Multnomah County announced that USPS began delivering ballots on April 29 for Oregon's May 19 primary, with voters expected to receive ballots by May 7. Ballots may be returned by mail (postmarked by Election Day) or via 30+ official drop sites and voter service centers.

PA.title: Shapiro Administration Reminds Voters That the Mail Ballot Application Deadline Is One Week Away
PA.summary: Secretary of the Commonwealth Al Schmidt reminded Pennsylvania voters that mail ballot applications must be submitted by 5 p.m. on May 12 for the May 19 primary, with more than 820,000 applications already received.

PA.title: Pa. primary election 2026: What you need to know about your Election Day voting rights
PA.summary: Spotlight PA outlined Pennsylvania voters' rights ahead of the May 19 primary, including ID requirements for first-time voters, provisional ballots, accessibility accommodations, polling-place protections against intimidation, and rules for voters with criminal convictions.

PA.title: Secure Ballot Drop-off Boxes Installed on April 28, 2026 for the May 2026 Primary Election
PA.summary: Northampton County deployed seven secure ballot drop-off boxes for the May 19 primary, including a 24-hour location at the 911 Center. Mail-in/civilian absentee ballot applications must be received by 5 p.m. on May 12.

RI.title: Rhode Island House Passes Bill Moving Presidential Primary from Late April to Early March
RI.summary: The Rhode Island House unanimously passed HB 7090 on April 30, moving the state's presidential primary from late April to early March beginning in 2028. The bill was referred to the Senate Judiciary Committee following passage and does not affect general-election ballot access deadlines.

SC.title: SC can send voter rolls to the federal government, Election Commission says
SC.summary: The South Carolina State Election Commission voted 4-1 on April 28 to share voter registration data — including names, birthdates, addresses, and the last four digits of Social Security numbers — with the U.S. Department of Justice. The agreement adds encryption and hashing safeguards and stipulates that voters flagged by DOJ will not be automatically removed from the rolls.

SC.title: South Carolina Election Commission agrees to share voter data with Department of Justice
SC.summary: WIS reported the SCEC's 4-1 vote to share voter registration data with the DOJ to help identify potential non-citizens or otherwise ineligible registrants. Officials said sensitive data fields will be transmitted using one-way hashing.

SC.title: SCVotes Sends Data to Feds
SC.summary: South Carolina's election commission transmitted the voter database covering 3.3 million registered voters to the U.S. DOJ following the memorandum of understanding approved April 28. The article notes the data was sent via federal encrypted file sharing with hashing for sensitive fields.

SD.title: South Dakota enacts proof of citizenship law, 20 other election bills in 2026 session
SD.summary: South Dakota's 2026 legislative session enacted 21 election-related bills, including SB 175, a documentary proof-of-citizenship requirement for new voter registrations. The state joins Florida and Utah in adopting such requirements during 2026.

SD.title: AG Files Ballot Explanation for Citizenship Voting Amendment
SD.summary: South Dakota Attorney General Marty Jackley filed a ballot explanation for proposed Constitutional Amendment J, which clarifies that only U.S. citizens may vote in state elections. A public comment period runs through May 8, with the amendment headed to the November 3 general election ballot.

SD.title: Confusion Over New SD Voter ID Rules as June 2 Primary Nears
SD.summary: South Dakota county auditors are inconsistently implementing the new SB 175 proof-of-citizenship requirement as the June 2 primary approaches and absentee voting is underway.

TN.title: Lee signs law requiring new citizenship vetting for voters if feds develop national database
TN.summary: Gov. Bill Lee signed legislation creating a new citizenship vetting process for Tennessee voter registration that takes effect in 2028 if the federal government makes a national non-citizen database available to county election officials.

TN.title: Tennessee redistricting proposal follows Supreme Court voting rights decision
TN.summary: Following the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais decision, Gov. Bill Lee called a special session for the GOP-controlled Tennessee legislature to redraw the state's congressional districts. Proposed changes would split Memphis's majority-Black 9th District.

TX.title: Christian Menefee and Al Green, rivals in TX-18, align on aim of strengthening voting rights
TX.summary: U.S. Reps. Christian Menefee and Al Green, both in the Democratic primary runoff for Texas' 18th Congressional District, expressed support for new federal legislation to counteract the U.S. Supreme Court's recent ruling that weakened the Voting Rights Act.

TX.title: Political parties in Texas choose how to run their primaries. Here's how that causes headaches for voters.
TX.summary: Reporting on how Texas political parties' wide latitude over primary administration led to voters showing up at wrong polling places in counties including Dallas, Williamson, and Eastland during the March 3 primary.

TX.title: Some Dallas County Republicans trying to revive precinct voting that created chaos in primary
TX.summary: Dallas County Republicans filed suit seeking to require precinct-based voting in the May 26 primary runoff, after countywide voting was eliminated for the March 3 primary.

TX.title: Houston-area voters are in the midst of three consecutive elections
TX.summary: Coverage of Harris County voters facing back-to-back early voting periods for May 2 local elections and the upcoming May 26 primary runoff.

UT.title: Utah voter group is 'determined to act as a firewall' against Trump's DOJ
UT.summary: The League of Women Voters of Utah moved to dismiss the Trump administration's lawsuit seeking access to detailed Utah voter data including dates of birth, Social Security numbers, and driver's license numbers.

VT.title: House passes Vermont Voter Protections Act
VT.summary: The Vermont House of Representatives passed S.298, the Vermont Voting Rights Act, which prohibits voting discrimination based on race, color, language minority status, or disability and creates new criminal penalties for election intimidation.

VT.title: Vermont House passes voting rights measure
VT.summary: The Vermont House passed S.298, which establishes a state-level Voting Rights Act with protections against discrimination and stronger penalties for election interference and intimidation.

VA.title: Thousands of Virginians will regain the right to vote next month
VA.summary: Following the King v. Youngkin federal court ruling, June 1, 2026 will be the first day many Virginians with felony convictions will be eligible to register to vote without needing a governor's individual approval.

VA.title: Expanded voting rights for former felons in Virginia set to begin next month
VA.summary: Reports on the upcoming expansion of voting rights for Virginians with prior felony convictions, set to begin June 1 after a federal court ruled the state's blanket disenfranchisement violated the 1870 Virginia Readmission Act.

VA.title: Virginia voters back redistricting amendment after months of legal and political battles
VA.summary: Virginia voters narrowly approved the proposed constitutional amendment allowing the legislature to redraw congressional districts, by a 50.7-49.3 percent margin out of 2.5 million ballots cast.

VA.title: Virginia Supreme Court upholds block on redistricting certification
VA.summary: The Supreme Court of Virginia denied Attorney General Jay Jones' request to lift a lower court's injunction blocking certification of the April 21 redistricting referendum results.

VA.title: State Supreme Court hears arguments to overturn redistricting referendum; now Virginia waits
VA.summary: The Virginia Supreme Court heard arguments on the constitutionality of the redistricting referendum and declined to lift the lower-court block preventing certification of the April 21 results.

WA.title: Washington legislators update state voting rights act, enact eight other election-related bills
WA.summary: Governor Bob Ferguson signed 10 election-related bills, including HB 1710 (creating an attorney general preclearance system for local election changes) and HB 1750 (expanding the state Voting Rights Act with disparate-impact protections).

WV.title: Early voting opens across West Virginia ahead of May 12 primary
WV.summary: Early in-person voting opened statewide on April 29 ahead of the May 12 primary, the first under tightened photo ID rules and a closed Republican primary.

WV.title: West Virginia legislators place citizenship requirement for voting on the ballot, enact 10 other election bills
WV.summary: West Virginia lawmakers placed SJR 9, a citizens-only voting amendment, on the November 2026 ballot and enacted 10 other election-related bills during the 2026 session.

WV.title: How to vote in Fayette County
WV.summary: Voter guide explaining new photo ID requirements, the closed Republican primary, and key dates ahead of West Virginia's May 12 primary election.

WI.title: Wisconsin Elections Commission overrules ballot-counting decisions in Madison and Mequon
WI.summary: The Wisconsin Elections Commission ordered Madison to exclude 23 late-arriving absentee ballots and ordered Mequon to count five absentee ballots that had been improperly rejected, requiring both cities to revise their April 7 Supreme Court election totals.

WI.title: Madison Told To Reject 23 Ballots, Mequon Voters Win A Recount
WI.summary: Coverage of the Wisconsin Elections Commission's directives to Madison and Mequon to revise their canvass results from the April 7 spring election.

WI.title: Commission orders Madison election recount over ballots
WI.summary: The Wisconsin Elections Commission directed Madison to redo its canvass after determining 23 absentee ballots were improperly counted.

WI.title: Liberals Gain Seat on Wisconsin Supreme Court, Adding to Firewall in Voting Cases
WI.summary: Chris Taylor's win expanded the Wisconsin Supreme Court's liberal majority to 5-2, the largest progressive margin in decades and a significant ruling for upcoming voting rights cases.

WY.title: Saturday Convention: Wyoming GOP OKs Loyalty Tests For Candidates, Will Sue State
WY.summary: At its state convention, the Wyoming Republican Party adopted bylaws creating a framework to vet, endorse, and financially back candidates ahead of the August primary, in defiance of state law, and announced plans to sue.

WY.title: Wyoming Republican Party plans to buck law and endorse candidates ahead of critical primary
WY.summary: The Wyoming Republican Party advanced new bylaws permitting endorsements and financial backing of candidates in primaries, contradicting state election law, ahead of the August 2026 primary.

WY.title: Statewide candidates split on Wyoming GOP's plans to defy state law and make endorsements
WY.summary: Wyoming statewide candidates expressed mixed reactions to the state Republican Party's plans to defy state law and endorse candidates ahead of the August primary.

DC.title: DC Board of Elections Ranked Choice Voting Townhall
DC.summary: The DC Board of Elections held a ranked choice voting townhall to educate voters ahead of the June 16 primary, the first DC election to use RCV.

DC.title: Major D.C. mayoral and congressional delegate debates set for May 2 at George Washington University
DC.summary: Coverage of upcoming DC mayoral and congressional delegate debates scheduled for May 2 at George Washington University, ahead of the open-seat June 16 primary.

DC.title: D.C. Election 2026: The Georgetowner's Guide to Mayoral Forums & Debates
DC.summary: Guide listing forthcoming DC mayoral candidate forums and televised debates ahead of the June 16 primary, the first open mayoral seat in 20 years and the first to use ranked-choice voting.

AK.title: Gov. Dunleavy introduces new elections bill days after vetoing last version
AK.summary: Gov. Dunleavy proposed a substitute elections bill with a new signature-verification process and delayed implementation past the November 2026 general election; legislative leaders said little time remains to act.

AK.title: Dunleavy introduces new elections bill days after vetoing a similar one - with 13 days left in session
AK.summary: The governor's revised election overhaul bill arrived with less than two weeks left in the regular session, drawing skepticism from lawmakers about its prospects.

AL.title: Alabama lawmakers pass plan for new U.S. House primary if courts allow different districts
AL.summary: Alabama legislators passed bills authorizing Gov. Kay Ivey to schedule a new congressional primary under revised districts if courts permit, while the May 19 primary proceeds under the current map.

AL.title: Alabama urges US Supreme Court to let it eliminate a Democratic-held congressional district
AL.summary: Alabama filed an emergency appeal at the U.S. Supreme Court seeking to revert to a congressional map with one majority-Black district, citing the Court's recent Louisiana v. Callais ruling weakening Voting Rights Act enforcement.

AL.title: Alabama Attorney General files motions with U.S. Supreme Court seeking to redistrict
AL.summary: Alabama AG Steve Marshall asked the Supreme Court to lift the injunction requiring two majority-Black congressional districts, with a response from plaintiffs requested by May 14.

AL.title: Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey signs primary bills as state seeks to redistrict
AL.summary: Gov. Ivey signed two bills allowing Alabama to set new primary dates for congressional and state Senate seats if federal courts permit use of previously contested maps.

AL.title: Federal court rejects Alabama's emergency request in redistricting case
AL.summary: A federal court denied Alabama's emergency motion to use a contested congressional map for the 2026 elections, leaving the state's bid pending before the U.S. Supreme Court.

AR.title: Little Rock Mayor Frank Scott Jr. announces campaign for a third term
AR.summary: Little Rock Mayor Frank Scott Jr. announced his bid for a third term, kicking off the city's 2026 mayoral race ahead of the November general election.

AZ.title: Supreme Court voting rights ruling set to reshape local power from statehouses to school boards
AZ.summary: Stateline analyzes how the Louisiana v. Callais ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act could affect map-drawing for state legislative, county and municipal districts in Arizona and other states.

AZ.title: May 19, 2026 Local Elections - Maricopa County
AZ.summary: Maricopa County is administering an all-mail jurisdictional election May 19 for Tempe City Council, the Town of Guadalupe property tax measure, and the Goldfield Ranch Fire District; the last day to mail ballots is May 12.

CA.title: In the six-way race to be California's treasurer, it likely comes down to two Democrats
CA.summary: CalMatters profiles the June 2 primary contest for state treasurer, focused on Lt. Gov. Eleni Kounalakis and state Sen. Anna Caballero in a six-candidate field.

CA.title: Attorney General Bonta and Secretary of State Weber: Vote Early in June Primary Election and Know Your Voting Rights
CA.summary: California's AG and Secretary of State urged voters to use early in-person voting and vote-by-mail for the June 2 primary, and outlined election integrity protections for poll workers and voters.

CT.title: On second try, absentee voting bill glides to passage in CT House
CT.summary: The Connecticut House passed HB 5001, the universal no-excuse absentee voting bill, on a 101-49 party-line vote, sending it to the Senate.

CT.title: Voting by mail to be a universal option in Connecticut
CT.summary: The Connecticut Senate passed HB 5001 25-11, sending universal no-excuse absentee voting to Gov. Ned Lamont's desk; the bill also restricts law enforcement near polling places and increases penalties for harassing election workers.

CT.title: Expanded Absentee Ballot Legislation Passes Legislature, Heads To Lamont
CT.summary: After November 2024 voters approved a constitutional change, lawmakers passed implementing legislation enabling absentee voting for any reason starting with the 2026 elections.

CT.title: All CT residents expected to be able to vote by mail this year
CT.summary: WSHU reports all Connecticut residents are expected to be able to vote by mail in 2026 once Gov. Lamont signs HB 5001, marking the state's transition to no-excuse absentee voting.

CT.title: CT lawmakers warn about threats to democracy at shadow hearing
CT.summary: Connecticut legislators held a shadow hearing on threats to election administration and voter access, citing federal pressures and state-level safeguards in current bills.

FL.title: Florida lawmakers pass a voting map that could help Republicans flip 4 House seats
FL.summary: The Florida Legislature approved a new congressional map that could give Republicans up to four additional U.S. House seats, with the state Senate passing it 21-17 hours after the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling weakened Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act.

FL.title: DeSantis signs Florida's new congressional map into law, lawsuit follows
FL.summary: Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the new congressional redistricting map into law, and within hours voting-rights groups filed the first of multiple lawsuits alleging the plan violates the state's Fair Districts Amendment.

FL.title: 3 lawsuits now filed to block new Florida congressional map after redistricting
FL.summary: Three separate lawsuits have been filed in Tallahassee state court challenging Florida's newly enacted congressional map, alleging the plan is an unconstitutional partisan gerrymander under the Fair Districts Amendment.

FL.title: Election leaders scrambling to inform voters on new congressional map amid lawsuits
FL.summary: County election supervisors are racing to update precinct boundaries and notify voters about their new congressional districts ahead of the August primary, even as litigation over the new map continues.

GA.title: Five candidates are running in the May 19 general election for three seats on the Georgia Supreme Court
GA.summary: Five candidates are competing in nonpartisan elections for three Georgia Supreme Court seats on the May 19 ballot, including incumbent justices Charlie Bethel and Sarah Hawkins Warren facing Democratic-backed challengers Miracle Rankin and Jen Jordan.

HI.title: This Rich Hawai'i Super PAC Is Already Shaping A Key Statewide Election
HI.summary: An investigative report on how the Pacific Resource Partnership super PAC is leveraging large independent expenditures to influence Hawaii's 2026 statewide and county races, including the lieutenant governor and Kauai mayoral contests.

IA.title: Democrats criticize Iowa decision to share voter info with US Justice Department
IA.summary: Democratic candidates for statewide office criticized Secretary of State Paul Pate and the Iowa AG for handing over voter registration data, including driver's license numbers and partial Social Security numbers, to the U.S. Department of Justice.

IA.title: Iowa voters share privacy concerns after state gives election records to the federal government
IA.summary: Iowa voters express privacy concerns after the Secretary of State's office sent voter registration records, including partial Social Security and driver's license numbers, to the U.S. Department of Justice.

ID.title: Friday is the deadline to request absentee ballots in Idaho ahead of 2026 primary election
ID.summary: Idaho voters have until 5 p.m. Friday, May 8 to pre-register online or request an absentee ballot for the May 19 primary; voters can still register in person at early voting locations or on Election Day with photo ID and proof of residence.

ID.title: Two candidates vie for seat in Idaho 1st Congressional District Democratic primary
ID.summary: Democrats Brungardt and Peterson are competing in the May 19 primary for the right to challenge the Republican incumbent in Idaho's 1st Congressional District.

ID.title: Three candidates challenge Risch in Republican primary election for U.S. Senate
ID.summary: Incumbent U.S. Sen. Jim Risch faces three Republican challengers (Joe Evans, Denny LaVe and Josh Roy) on the May 19 GOP primary ballot for Idaho's U.S. Senate seat.

IL.title: Proposed Illinois referendum protecting redistricting paused after Supreme Court voting rights ruling weakens Civil Rights-era law
IL.summary: Illinois Senate Democrats tabled a proposed constitutional amendment on redistricting after the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling, with leaders saying they need time to assess the decision's impact on minority-representation protections.

IN.title: Trump-Backed Candidates Dominate Indiana Elections After Incumbents Opposed Redistricting
IN.summary: Five Republican Indiana state senators who voted against Trump's congressional redistricting push were ousted in the May 5 primary by Trump-endorsed challengers, potentially reopening the door to a renewed redistricting effort.

KS.title: Leawood pastor Adam Hamilton enters Kansas U.S. Senate race as Democrat to challenge Marshall
KS.summary: Resurrection Church pastor Adam Hamilton announced his Democratic candidacy for U.S. Senate, joining a crowded field challenging Republican incumbent Roger Marshall ahead of the August 4, 2026 primary.

KS.title: Kansas pastor enters U.S. Senate race as Democrat, wants to give Roger Marshall an early retirement
KS.summary: Adam Hamilton officially launched his Democratic Senate bid, criticizing Marshall on affordability and tariffs, as up to eight Democrats compete in the August 4 primary for the Kansas Senate seat.

KS.title: Late entry, big money — Leawood pastor Adam Hamilton upends Kansas Democratic Senate primary
KS.summary: Political analysts assess Adam Hamilton's chances of flipping the Kansas Senate seat in a state that has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932.

KY.title: A 2026 Primary Election Guide from WKMS
KY.summary: Voter guide for Kentucky's May 19, 2026 primary, covering the open U.S. Senate race to replace retiring Mitch McConnell, the 4th congressional district race, and state legislative contests.

KY.title: How we made Kentucky's 2026 primary election voter guide
KY.summary: LPM details the methodology behind its 2026 Kentucky primary voter guide, covering the May 19 closed primary and key races including 12 GOP and 7 Democratic candidates for U.S. Senate.

KY.title: Kentucky's 2026 primary election voter guide
KY.summary: Statewide voter guide explaining Kentucky's closed primary system, polling hours, and candidate fields for the open Senate seat and 4th district House race ahead of the May 19 primary.

KY.title: Early voting in NKY starts today: What you need to know
KY.summary: Northern Kentucky in-person excused absentee voting opened May 6, with no-excuse early voting May 14-16 ahead of the May 19 primary; absentee ballots must be received by 6 p.m. on Election Day.

LA.title: Louisiana's start to US House redistricting riles lawmakers, voting rights crowd
LA.summary: The Senate and Governmental Affairs Committee held a contentious public hearing on a new congressional map after the Supreme Court struck down the existing map; Republican proposals to eliminate one or both majority-Black districts drew protests and a NAACP leader was restrained by sergeants-at-arms.

LA.title: Louisiana map fight erupts at Capitol after Supreme Court ruling
LA.summary: Hundreds packed the State Capitol as the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee took testimony on competing congressional maps, with options including a 5-1, 6-0, or current 4-2 majority-Black configuration.

LA.title: Senate committee to hear congressional redistricting testimony Friday
LA.summary: Preview of the Louisiana Senate Governmental Affairs Committee hearing on a new congressional map, following Gov. Landry's suspension of the May 16 U.S. House primaries after the Supreme Court's Callais ruling.

LA.title: Louisiana used unconstitutional US House maps for past elections. Why not now?
LA.summary: Analysis of why Louisiana's U.S. House primaries were suspended this cycle following the Supreme Court ruling on the state's congressional map, in contrast to past elections held under maps later found unconstitutional.

MA.title: In reversal, Mass. AG blocks legislative stipend ballot question from moving forward
MA.summary: Massachusetts Attorney General Andrea Campbell's office notified the Secretary of State that an initiative petition to overhaul legislative stipends cannot proceed to the 2026 ballot, after a Supreme Judicial Court advisory opinion deemed it unconstitutional.

MA.title: The 11 ballot questions Mass. voters might face
MA.summary: After lawmakers let the May 6 deadline pass without acting on any of the 11 certified initiatives, supporters of measures on rent control, same-day voter registration, the income tax, public records and more must now collect additional signatures to reach the November ballot.

MD.title: Maryland Senate President Bill Ferguson faces tough race after opposing redistricting
MD.summary: Maryland Senate President Bill Ferguson faces his most competitive primary challenge after blocking a redistricting bill backed by Gov. Moore that would have redrawn Maryland's congressional map ahead of 2026.

MD.title: Is redistricting dead in Maryland?
MD.summary: Sen. Arthur Ellis is still pushing Senate leadership to act on a special session for redistricting, but party leaders indicate no special session or new map will occur this year for Maryland's congressional districts.

MD.title: Endorsement snubs, rethinking redistricting, public campaign fund feuds, in political notes
MD.summary: Roundup of Maryland election developments including post-Callais redistricting reconsideration, endorsement decisions, and disputes over the state's public campaign financing system ahead of the June 23 primary.

MD.title: Supreme Court voting rights ruling set to reshape local power from statehouses to school boards
MD.summary: Stateline analysis of how the Callais ruling affects state and local elections, noting Maryland's just-signed Voting Rights Act of 2026 (SB 255) as a potential safeguard for local voting rights protections.

MD.title: Maryland Passed Its State Voting Rights Act 24 Hours Before the SCOTUS Callais Decision
MD.summary: Maryland's new state Voting Rights Act took effect one day before the Supreme Court's Callais ruling weakened federal racial-gerrymandering protections, raising questions about whether state VRAs can fill the gap.

ME.title: In-person absentee voting begins Monday ahead of Maine primary
ME.summary: In-person absentee voting for Maine's June 9, 2026 primary opens May 11; ranked-choice voting will be used for federal primaries and unenrolled voters may participate in either party primary.

ME.title: In-person absentee voting begins Monday, May 11 for June 9 Primary Election
ME.summary: Secretary of State announcement that in-person absentee voting begins May 11 and ends June 4 for the June 9 primary, with absentee ballots due by 8 p.m. on Election Day.

MI.title: Election results: May 2026 special general election in Southeast Michigan
MI.summary: Live results from the May 2026 special and general elections across Southeast Michigan, including school bond proposals and millage questions decided by voters across multiple counties.

MN.title: Supreme Court guts Voting Rights Act, what it means for Minnesota
MN.summary: After the U.S. Supreme Court's 6-3 ruling in Louisiana v. Callais weakened Section 2 of the federal Voting Rights Act, Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison and voting-rights advocates say the state's own Voting Rights Act and same-day registration system are now even more important for protecting Minnesota voters.

MO.title: Signatures submitted for Missouri initiative requiring voter approval for certain legislative changes to initiative process and voter-approved laws
MO.summary: The Respect Missouri Voters campaign submitted more than 367,000 signatures to the Missouri Secretary of State for a proposed constitutional amendment that would declare initiative and referendum rights fundamental and require an 80% legislative supermajority before lawmakers could refer changes to voter-approved laws back to the ballot.

MS.title: Mississippi special session to focus on Supreme Court redistricting
MS.summary: Gov. Tate Reeves called a May 20 special legislative session to redraw Mississippi's state Supreme Court districts after the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling altered federal Voting Rights Act protections.

MS.title: Temporary House move to Old Capitol draws mixed reactions from lawmakers
MS.summary: Mississippi House members will convene at the Old Capitol building for the May 20 redistricting special session, a decision Black lawmakers criticized as tone-deaf given the building's history with the 1890 constitution that disenfranchised Black voters.

MS.title: Rep. Thompson to 'fight until Hell freezes over' against Miss. redistricting
MS.summary: U.S. Rep. Bennie Thompson said he will fight any GOP push to redraw Mississippi's majority-Black 2nd Congressional District, calling the effort racially motivated as Republicans cite the U.S. Supreme Court's Callais decision to argue for new congressional maps.

MS.title: Congressman Bennie Thompson calls redistricting push racially motivated
MS.summary: Rep. Bennie Thompson denounced calls from state Republicans and the Trump administration to dismantle Mississippi's 2nd Congressional District, saying he will fight any redistricting plan in court as racially discriminatory.

MT.title: New voting rules in play as primary election begins
MT.summary: As Montana's June 2 primary voting gets underway, county election administrators are walking voters through new requirements from the 2025 legislative session, including a photo ID requirement at polling places, a new mail-ballot rule that voters must write their birth year on the return envelope, and the elimination of Monday-before-Election-Day registration; multiple voting-rights lawsuits challenging the laws remain pending.

NC.title: NC registration repair project has resolved 36,000 voter registrations
NC.summary: The North Carolina State Board of Elections' registration repair project has resolved more than 36,000 incomplete voter registration records since launching last summer, dropping the statewide total of incomplete records from 103,329 to 66,658 by April 29.

ND.title: Write-in candidate could take late North Dakota legislator's spot in general election
ND.summary: Potential candidates to replace the late Rep. Liz Conmy as the Democratic-NPL House nominee in District 11 have until May 19 to file as a certified write-in candidate with the North Dakota Secretary of State.

ND.title: Mail-in ballots for North Dakota June primary now available
ND.summary: North Dakota election officials began mailing absentee ballots for the June 9 primary on April 30, and a stricter new deadline requires all mail-in ballots to be received by Election Day, replacing the prior postmark-and-grace-period rule.

ND.title: New Ballot Measure Guide to Be Sent to Voters Ahead of June 9 Primary Election
ND.summary: The North Dakota Secretary of State announced that a ballot measure guide for statewide Measure #1 (the single-subject rule for constitutional amendments) was mailed April 24 to roughly 450,000 active voter households.

ND.title: Five statewide candidate filing deadlines in the next two weeks
ND.summary: Ballotpedia notes North Dakota's May 19 primary write-in candidate filing deadline among five upcoming statewide candidate filing deadlines around the country.

NE.title: Nebraska's 'blue dot' becomes the center of a closely watched Democratic primary fight

John Cavanaugh would risk the state's split electoral-vote system, with rival Denise Powell arguing his departure would let the GOP-controlled legislature scrap the 'blue dot' and switch Nebraska to winner-take-all.

NJ.title: New Jersey election 2026: Primary voter guides, key races and more
NJ.summary: WHYY's voter guide previews the June 2 New Jersey primary, including the U.S. Senate race, all 12 U.S. House contests, and key voter deadlines such as the May 12 registration deadline and May 26-31 early voting window.

NJ.title: Gov. Sherrill eyes redistricting in NJ after controversial voting rights decision
NJ.summary: Gov. Mikie Sherrill said New Jersey is considering a mid-decade congressional redistricting in response to the U.S. Supreme Court's recent ruling weakening Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act.

NJ.title: Livingston Township Sets May 12 Deadline for Primary Election Voter Registration
NJ.summary: Livingston Township and other New Jersey municipalities are reminding residents that the deadline to register to vote in the June 2 primary election is Tuesday, May 12, 2026.

NM.title: New Mexico Election 2026: trail notes

NM.title: Independent voting off to slow start in New Mexico's first semi-open primary election

NM.title: 2026 Primary Election Update
NM.summary: Bernalillo County Clerk Michelle Kavanaugh reports more than 21,000 absentee ballots were requested by May 5 and outlines key June 2 primary deadlines, including May 19 to request an absentee ballot and May 16 expanded early voting.

NM.title: Early voting opens strong in Dona Ana County as New Mexico primary season begins
NM.summary: Dona Ana County reports strong turnout in the first days of in-person early voting and absentee ballot returns for the June 2 New Mexico primary, the first under the state's new semi-open primary system.

NV.title: Three Democrats drop out of northern Nevada races, but will remain on the primary ballot
NV.summary: Three Democratic candidates have withdrawn from northern Nevada legislative contests but their names will still appear on the June 9 primary ballot because they exited after the March 24 candidate withdrawal deadline.

NY.title: Governor Hochul Delivers Remarks on New York's Redistricting Plans Amid Trump Administration's Nationwide Gerrymandering Push

NY.title: Democrats want to redraw New York's map - their own state law may not let them
