OH.title: Ohio Democrats nearly matched GOP primary turnout. Does it matter for November?
OH.summary: Ohio Democrats requested 791,355 primary ballots versus 817,159 Republican ballots in the May 5 primary, a sharp rebound from 2022's 2-to-1 GOP advantage and the highest Democratic primary turnout in a midterm year since 2006.

OH.title: Ohio sees small uptick in voter turnout during May primary; what to expect in November election
OH.summary: Statewide turnout in Ohio's May 5 primary was about 22.6% of registered voters, up from 20.8% in 2022, with roughly 122,000 more votes cast even as voter rolls shrank by about 50,000.

OR.title: Clackamas County voters should have received their ballots for the May 19, 2026 Primary Election
OR.summary: Clackamas County Elections notified voters that ballots mailed April 29 should have arrived, and reminded those who haven't received one to contact the elections office, with ballots due back by 8 p.m. on May 19.

PA.title: Pennsylvania mail ballot dating rules have been in flux for years. Here is what you need to know.
PA.summary: Pennsylvania counties currently cannot reject mail ballots that lack a proper handwritten date on the return envelope after recent state and federal court rulings, though both decisions are under appeal and election officials still recommend voters fill in the date.

PA.title: Pa. primary election 2026: How to vote, where to vote, and everything you need to know for May 19
PA.summary: A guide to Pennsylvania's May 19 primary covers polling hours (7 a.m.-8 p.m.), mail ballot request deadlines (May 12), ID rules for first-time voters, and what's on the ballot, including races for governor, lieutenant governor, the entire state House, half the state Senate, and all 17 congressional districts.

SC.title: SC House panel approves 2-month delay in congressional primary amid redistricting push
SC.summary: A South Carolina House panel voted 3-2 along party lines to advance legislation moving the state's June 9 congressional primary to August 11 to allow time to redraw the state's seven U.S. House districts, a delay that election officials estimate would cost taxpayers at least $2.2 million.

SC.title: White House map of SC voting lines could help Democrats, GOP leader warns
SC.summary: South Carolina House GOP leaders circulated a White House-backed congressional map that would draw U.S. Rep. Jim Clyburn out of the district he has represented for 34 years; Senate Majority Leader Shane Massey warned the map could put traditionally Republican districts in play for Democrats.

SC.title: SC House Republicans vote to consider congressional redistricting after Trump White House pressure
SC.summary: The South Carolina House voted 87-25 along party lines to add congressional redistricting to a resolution governing what the legislature can do after the regular session ends May 14, opening the door to a mid-decade map redraw at the urging of the Trump White House.

SD.title: South Dakota voter registration deadline is May 18
SD.summary: Secretary of State Monae Johnson reminded South Dakotans that the deadline to register to vote in the June 2 primary is 5 p.m. local time on May 18, and outlined the state and county offices and agencies where residents can register or update their information.

SD.title: South Dakota voters reminded to register or update info by May 18 for June primary
SD.summary: KOTA reported on the upcoming May 18 voter registration deadline for South Dakota's June 2 primary, including a reminder that under SB 175 first-time registrants must now provide proof of U.S. citizenship as part of the application.

TN.title: Tennessee Republicans pass a map to break up the state's lone Democratic House seat
TN.summary: Tennessee's GOP-led legislature approved a new congressional map that carves up the majority-Black 9th District in Memphis, eliminating the state's lone Democratic-held seat ahead of the 2026 elections.

TN.title: NAACP Tennessee files lawsuit challenging redrawn US House district map
TN.summary: The NAACP's Tennessee chapter filed an emergency petition in Davidson County Chancery Court hours after Gov. Bill Lee signed the new map, arguing the mid-decade redistricting violates state statutory and constitutional law.

TN.title: Tennessee lawmakers approve new House map to eliminate Democratic-held seat
TN.summary: Republican lawmakers approved and Gov. Lee signed a new congressional map dividing the Memphis-based 9th District; candidates have until May 15 to qualify under the new lines.

TN.title: Tennessee approves new congressional map in latest redistricting flurry
TN.summary: Tennessee becomes the latest state to push through a mid-decade redistricting plan, redrawing all nine U.S. House districts to favor Republicans ahead of the August primary.

TN.title: Another legal challenge to Tennessee's new congressional map
TN.summary: A coalition of voters and Democratic congressional candidates filed a federal lawsuit challenging Tennessee's new congressional map, marking the second legal challenge in two days.

TX.title: Ken Paxton narrowly leads John Cornyn in new poll of Texas' Senate GOP runoff
TX.summary: A University of Houston poll shows Attorney General Ken Paxton leading Sen. John Cornyn 48% to 45% with 7% undecided shortly before early voting begins in the May 26 Republican primary runoff.

TX.title: Texas' Republican Senate primary runoff statistically tied shortly before start of early voting, poll finds
TX.summary: With early voting starting May 18, polling shows the Cornyn-Paxton GOP Senate runoff in a statistical dead heat ahead of the May 26 primary runoff election.

VA.title: Supreme Court of Virginia strikes down redistricting amendment, keeps current maps in place
VA.summary: The Virginia Supreme Court voided the April 21 voter-approved redistricting amendment, ruling lawmakers violated the multistep amendment process and ordering use of existing congressional maps for 2026.

VA.title: Court rejects Virginia redistricting in a blow to Democrats' counter to Trump, GOP
VA.summary: The Virginia Supreme Court struck down a voter-approved constitutional amendment that would have allowed mid-decade redistricting, dealing a setback to Democrats' efforts to counter GOP redistricting in other states.

VA.title: Virginia's Supreme Court tosses voter-approved redistricting plan in blow to Democrats
VA.summary: The state's high court found the legislature violated procedural rules for ballot amendments and ordered Virginia to keep using its existing congressional districts for the 2026 elections.

VA.title: Expanded voting rights for former felons in Virginia set to begin next month
VA.summary: Beginning June 1, thousands of Virginians with felony convictions will be able to register to vote without first needing the governor's approval, following a court ruling that found the state's restoration process violated a Civil War-era law.

WA.title: Candidate filing begins, kicking off Washington election season
WA.summary: Official Candidate Filing Week opened May 4 in Washington, with candidates filing for federal, state, judicial and local races ahead of the August 4 primary and November 3 general election.

WA.title: 2026 Candidate Filing Week underway
WA.summary: Washington candidates have through 5 p.m. Friday May 8 to file declarations of candidacy with the Secretary of State for federal, state and judicial offices appearing on the August primary ballot.

WA.title: Controversial ex-WA lawmaker attempts comeback for Republican-held seat
WA.summary: Former state Rep. Robert Sutherland is running to succeed retiring Rep. Carolyn Eslick in the 39th Legislative District, one of several intra-party matchups expected on Washington's 2026 ballot.

WV.title: More than 48,000 ballots already cast in WV as early voting is slated to end at 5 p.m. on Saturday
WV.summary: More than 48,200 West Virginia voters had cast ballots in the first 10 days of early voting ahead of the May 12 primary, with new photo ID requirements in effect for the first time.

WV.title: Early voting continues for West Virginia primary election
WV.summary: Early in-person voting in West Virginia's May 12 primary continues through May 9, with polling places open in all 55 counties; voters must show photo ID under new rules.

WV.title: Here's what more than 200 West Virginians say they want to hear from candidates this election season
WV.summary: A Mountain State Spotlight survey of more than 200 voters ahead of the May 12 primary found data centers, schools and the economy among the top issues voters want candidates to address.

WV.title: West Virginia Election Day Happens Tuesday
WV.summary: West Virginia's primary election is Tuesday, May 12, with U.S. Senate, House, state legislative and county races on the ballot and new photo ID requirements in effect.

WY.title: Election time
WY.summary: Hulett's municipal election will be held Tuesday, May 12, with voters choosing a mayor and two council members; the article also previews the upcoming statewide candidate filing period that opens May 14.

AL.title: Supreme Court hands Alabama major boost in redistricting fight
AL.summary: The Supreme Court cleared the way for Alabama to adopt its 2023 GOP-drawn congressional map for the 2026 elections; Justice Sotomayor's dissent warned the change 'will cause only confusion as Alabamians begin to vote in the elections scheduled for next week.'

AL.title: Redistricting updates: Alabama, South Carolina, Missouri
AL.summary: Following the SCOTUS ruling, Gov. Kay Ivey called an Aug. 11 special primary for the 1st, 2nd, 6th and 7th congressional districts; votes cast May 19 in those races will be tabulated and made public.

AL.title: Decision 2026: What Alabama primary voters need to know
AL.summary: Voter guide ahead of the May 19 Alabama statewide primary covering gubernatorial, statewide constitutional officer, and local races.

AK.title: It's bill-passing season. Here's what to expect in the final days of the Alaska Legislature's session.
AK.summary: Overview of bills moving in the final days of the legislative session, including discussion of the failed SB 64 elections reform package and remaining election-related measures.

CA.title: Panicked California Democrats are pushing a risky strategy: Wait ‘til the last minute to vote
CA.summary: Reports on a strategy by some California Democrats to delay returning ballots in the crowded governor's primary, raising concerns about a top-two GOP sweep and longer counts.

CO.title: Move over Election Day. Colorado is about to start having election month.
CO.summary: HB 26-1113, which would let county clerks begin mailing ballots 29 days before Election Day (up from 22), cleared the legislature and was headed to Gov. Polis amid concerns about USPS delays.

FL.title: What you need to know about Central Florida election safety, security ahead of the 2026 midterm elections
FL.summary: Three Central Florida supervisors of elections (Orange, Seminole, Osceola) held a public panel on 2026 election security, addressing ICE concerns at polling sites, armed individuals near polls, and poll-worker training plans.

FL.title: New congressional maps in Florida, Tennessee aim to shift five more districts to Republicans ahead of 2026 midterms
FL.summary: Florida became the eighth state to draw a new congressional map for the 2026 cycle after Gov. DeSantis signed the new map May 4, 2026; the map redraws 21 of 28 districts and faces three pending Fair Districts lawsuits.

GA.title: Georgia early voting turnout breaks records ahead of May 19 election
GA.summary: More than 480,000 early and absentee ballots had been cast as of May 8 ahead of the May 19 primary, with turnout pacing 28% above 2022.

GA.title: Georgia elections: Early Voting for primary and runoff races ends Friday, May 15
GA.summary: Outlines the May 15 close of advance voting before the May 19 primary, with reminders on ID requirements, polling locations, and the role of these contests in selecting nominees for statewide offices.

HI.title: Legislators mull bill to neuter corporate influence on elections

HI.title: Tax cuts preserved, immigration enforcement limited as Legislature sends final bills to Green
HI.summary: End-of-session wrap that includes SB 2471 (corporate election spending ban) among the final bills sent to Gov. Green, with the campaign-finance measure highlighted as a signature piece of the 2026 session.

HI.title: Hawaii constitutional amendment on RISE bonds referred to November 2026 ballot
HI.summary: Hawaii lawmakers placed a constitutional amendment authorizing Resilient Infrastructure for Shelter and Equity (RISE) bonds on the November 2026 ballot, joining the Simple-Majority and Senate-judicial-confirmation amendments already qualified.

ID.title: Three Democrats to vie for Idaho U.S. Senate seat held by Risch
ID.summary: Three Democrats — Nickolas 'Bonds, Brad Moore, and David Roth — are competing in the May 19 primary for the U.S. Senate seat held by Republican Sen. Jim Risch.

ID.title: Idaho campaign finance: Boise Democrat tops list of legislative campaign fundraisers
ID.summary: Rep. Steve Berch, D-Boise, has raised the most money of any legislative candidate in 2026, according to Idaho campaign finance records reviewed ahead of the May 19 primary.

IL.title: Right-wing group sues Illinois in first post-Callais attack on a state Voting Rights Act

IN.title: Primary turnout is up in Marion County, but Indiana's voting numbers remain consistently low
IN.summary: Voter turnout in the May 5 primary reached about 15.8% in Marion County — the highest rate for a midterm primary since at least 2010 — though statewide turnout remains consistently low.

KS.title: Kansas Democrat Sharice Davids makes reelection campaign for U.S. House seat official
KS.summary: U.S. Rep. Sharice Davids filed for reelection in the 3rd Congressional District at the Secretary of State's office in Topeka, seeking a fifth term after declining to run for U.S. Senate.

KY.title: Early voting underway in Butler County ahead of Kentucky primaries
KY.summary: Excused early voting is underway at the Butler County courthouse ahead of Kentucky's May 19 primary; no-excuse early voting runs May 14-16.

KY.title: Democrats make their pitches in Kentucky's Senate race
KY.summary: Democratic candidates for U.S. Senate made their final pitches to voters one week before Kentucky's May 19 primary, with the winner advancing to face the GOP nominee for the seat held by retiring Sen. Mitch McConnell.

KY.title: Kentucky Primary Election 2026: What voters need to know
KY.summary: Overview of Kentucky's May 19 primary, including poll hours (6 a.m.-6 p.m.), excused absentee dates (May 6-8, 11-13), and no-excuse early voting (May 14-16).

LA.title: Louisiana state redistricting issue spurs early voter turnout, absentee voting by Democrats
LA.summary: Early voting data shows Democrats outpaced Republicans by nearly 4,500 votes in the first seven days of Louisiana's May 16 election; analysts attributed the surge to the Callais ruling and the suspended U.S. House primaries.

LA.title: Two reminders that the rules of the 2026 election are still in flux
LA.summary: Analysis of how Louisiana's suspended U.S. House primaries and pending redistricting fights, alongside Alabama and Tennessee actions, may still reshape 2026 election rules.

LA.title: Angry voters and closed primaries: A preview of Election Day on May 16

ME.title: Absentee voting has started in the Maine primary. Here's what you need to know.
ME.summary: Absentee voting is underway for Maine's June 9 primary; the article explains who can vote, how to request and return ballots, and how ranked-choice voting will likely decide the competitive gubernatorial race.

MD.title: New MD law aims to protect voting rights
MD.summary: Maryland enacted the Maryland Voting Rights Act of 2026 (SB 255), signed by Gov. Wes Moore on April 28, prohibiting counties and municipalities from using electoral methods that dilute minority voters' power.

MI.title: Greene wins Michigan Senate special election, Democrats retain control of chamber
MI.summary: Democrat Chedrick Greene defeated Republican Jason Tunney with about 60% of the vote in the 35th Senate District special election, giving Democrats a 20-18 majority in the chamber through the rest of 2026.

MI.title: Democrats keep control of Michigan state Senate after special election win
MI.summary: National coverage of Greene's victory framed the result as a momentum signal for Democrats in a battleground state ahead of the November midterms.

MN.title: House passes elections bill after lengthy amendments discussions
MN.summary: The Minnesota House passed HF4240 by a 119-15 vote, an elections-administration bill that modernizes the statewide voter registration system, reimburses counties for special-election costs, and clarifies early-voting procedures.

MO.title: State Supreme Court upholds 'Missouri First' congressional map
MO.summary: The Missouri Supreme Court unanimously ruled that the GOP-drawn 'Missouri First' congressional map is in effect for the 2026 elections and rejected three constitutional challenges based on compactness and the pending referendum.

MO.title: Missouri Supreme Court upholds gerrymandered congressional map for August primary
MO.summary: Missouri Independent's coverage notes the AG's office defense and the practical effect: the map will be used for the August 4 primary, with the referendum process unable to suspend the law's implementation.

MT.title: Judge blocks Election Day voter registration changes
MT.summary: Lewis and Clark District Judge Adam Larsen enjoined SB 490, the 2025 law that would have cut off Election Day voter registration at noon for federal races, finding it would disproportionately harm Native American and young voters.

MT.title: Montana district court blocks law restricting voter registration hours, allows voter ID law
MT.summary: The same ruling denied the plaintiffs' motion to block SB 276, the tightened voter-ID law, with Judge Larsen writing that no evidence yet shows an eligible voter has been denied the right to vote under it.

NE.title: Burbank wins Nebraska Dem U.S. Senate primary, likely giving Osborn a clearer shot against Ricketts
NE.summary: Cindy Burbank won the Democratic U.S. Senate primary on May 12 but is expected to drop out so independent Dan Osborn can face Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts in November; Ricketts won the GOP nomination.

NE.title: Nebraska governor primary election results 2026 live updates
NE.summary: Incumbent Republican Gov. Jim Pillen won his primary against five challengers; former state Sen. Lynne Walz won the Democratic nomination, setting up the November matchup.

NV.title: Secretary of State releases polling locations for Primaries
NV.summary: The Nevada Secretary of State released polling locations for the June 9 primary. Early voting begins May 23 and runs through June 5.

NM.title: Independent voting off to slow start in New Mexico's first semi-open primary election
NM.summary: Independent voters comprised less than 10% of early ballots in the opening days of New Mexico's first semi-open primary, despite making up about 26% of the state's registered voters.

NY.title: New York Democrats unveil their own mid-decade redistricting scheme, targeting future elections
NY.summary: New York Democratic leaders, joined by U.S. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, met to advance a legislatively referred constitutional amendment that would allow mid-decade congressional redistricting if another state redraws first; the amendment requires two consecutive sessions and a public vote, meaning new maps would not take effect until 2028.

ND.title: North Dakota representative says process creates confusion during election cycle
ND.summary: U.S. Rep. Julie Fedorchak said she opposes mid-cycle redistricting as states elsewhere consider redrawing congressional maps, arguing the practice creates voter confusion; her comments come a month before North Dakota's June 9 primary.

OH.title: Gas, groceries and getting by: How voters in one Ohio district see affordability
OH.summary: NPR reports from a competitive Ohio congressional district following the May 5 primary, finding that affordability tops voters' concerns heading into the November midterm.

OH.title: How changes to Ohio's voting laws affected the May 2026 election
OH.summary: Ohio's May 5 primary was the first test of SB 293's elimination of the four-day post-Election-Day mail-ballot grace period; Secretary of State Frank LaRose reported turnout of about 20.14%.

OR.title: OPB's First Look: Oregon's primary election is a week away
OR.summary: With the May 19 primary one week out, OPB previews the contests including the governor's race, U.S. House seats, and Measure 120 (referendum on transportation funding).

OR.title: Lane County ballot return rate is right at state average
OR.summary: As of May 12, the statewide ballot return rate for Oregon's May 19 primary was 11.5%; Lane County's rate was 11.36%, near the state average, with Wallowa County leading at 21.88%.

PA.title: Pennsylvania won’t test internet-connected e-pollbooks in 2026 primary
PA.summary: The Pennsylvania Department of State has delayed its pilot of internet-connected electronic pollbooks until at least 2027, citing unresolved technical questions and low county interest after only three counties enrolled.

PA.title: Pennsylvania 2026 Primary: Tuesday, May 12 is deadline for absentee ballot, mail-in requests
PA.summary: Pennsylvania voters had until 5 p.m. on Tuesday, May 12, to submit mail-in or absentee ballot applications for the May 19 primary; completed ballots must be received by county election offices by 8 p.m. on Election Day.

SC.title: South Carolina lawmakers reject for now Trump's push to eliminate James Clyburn's seat
SC.summary: The South Carolina state Senate voted 29-17 on May 12, falling two votes short of the two-thirds majority needed to advance a redistricting resolution targeting Rep. James Clyburn's 6th District; five Republicans broke with party leadership.

SC.title: Rep. Clyburn says he is running for reelection 'irrespective' of South Carolina redistricting result
SC.summary: Rep. James Clyburn said he will seek reelection regardless of how South Carolina redraws its congressional districts, expressing confidence he could win even with fewer African American constituents.

SD.title: New laws result in 1,500 federal-only voter registrations ahead of South Dakota primary election
SD.summary: Approximately 1,500 South Dakotans have been registered as 'federal-only' voters ahead of the June 2 primary under new laws including SB 175, which requires documentary proof of citizenship for new registrants.

SD.title: South Dakota Secretary of State opens satellite voting locations in Lyman, Jackson, Todd, five other counties
SD.summary: Eight South Dakota counties — Lyman, Jackson, Todd, Bennett, Buffalo, Lawrence, Oglala Lakota, and Pennington — have established satellite absentee voting locations for the June 2 primary, expanding access in rural and tribal areas.

TN.title: ACLU sues to block redrawn Tennessee congressional map that breaks up Memphis
TN.summary: The ACLU and ACLU of Tennessee filed a federal lawsuit alleging intentional racial discrimination and First Amendment retaliation in the redrawn congressional map, on behalf of three Memphis voters and several civic organizations.

TN.title: Hearing set for TN Democrats' lawsuit against redistricting maps. Here's what to know.
TN.summary: A federal court set a May 20 hearing on Tennessee Democrats' challenge to the newly enacted congressional map; the hearing falls five days after the May 15 candidate qualifying deadline for the new districts.

TX.title: The Supreme Court's voting rights decision could reshape local government across Texas
TX.summary: Following the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling weakening Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, Texas advocates warn the decision could roll back decades of gains for Latino and Black representation on city councils and school boards.

UT.title: At-risk Utah voters have until May 6 to protect their information
UT.summary: Under SB 153, Utah voters in qualifying categories had until May 6 to apply for 'at-risk' status before approximately 1.3 million voters' registration data becomes public on May 26; sensitive data such as SSN remain private.

VT.title: Vermont lawmakers consider suspending new fines for candidates who don't disclose their finances
VT.summary: Vermont lawmakers advanced a bill to suspend enforcement of the state's candidate financial-disclosure penalty through May 30, 2027, citing confusion over the form's rollout and insufficient enforcement staffing.

VT.title: Lawmakers push to postpone Vermont disclosure fines
VT.summary: Coverage of the legislative push to defer candidate financial disclosure penalties for the 2026 cycle, with the House Government Operations Committee passing the revised bill without opposition.

VA.title: After SCOTUS voting rights ruling, Virginia leaders warn minority representation could erode
VA.summary: Virginia officials and advocates warn that the U.S. Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling weakening Section 2 of the VRA could erode Black political representation in Virginia, particularly in Northern Virginia, Richmond, and Hampton Roads.

VA.title: Headlines from across the state: After U.S. Supreme Court voting rights ruling, Virginia leaders warn minority representation could erode; more
VA.summary: Roundup coverage including how the Callais ruling weakening VRA Section 2 is being received by Virginia officials and what it could mean for state legislative and local redistricting going forward.

WA.title: A dozen legislative races to watch as Washington's election season revs up
WA.summary: With candidate filing week underway, the Standard profiles roughly a dozen competitive 2026 legislative races, including open seats created by 14 House and 5 Senate retirements ahead of the Aug. 4 primary.

WA.title: Washington state 2026 mid-term elections are off! May the odds be ever in your favor
WA.summary: Reports on the close of Washington's May 4-8 candidate filing week, with more than 1,000 candidates filing for 600-plus federal, state, and local offices ahead of the Aug. 4 primary.

WV.title: West Virginia voters navigate new law requiring photo IDs at polling places in primary election
WV.summary: West Virginia's HB 3016 photo-ID requirement was enforced for the first time during the May 12 primary, and election officials reported very few glitches as voters adjusted to the stricter ID rules.

WV.title: 2026 Primary Election: Incumbents show strength in local, state races
WV.summary: Statewide live-update coverage of West Virginia's May 12 primary, reporting that early-voting turnout of 67,356 ballots was about 8% higher than the 2022 primary's early total of 62,283.

WI.title: Will the Supreme Court's ruling on the Voting Rights Act impact Wisconsin's maps?
WI.summary: Analysis story examining how a recent U.S. Supreme Court ruling on Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act could affect future challenges to Wisconsin's legislative and congressional maps.

WY.title: Registered to vote? Over 2,800 Natrona County voters purged; party declaration deadline is Wednesday
WY.summary: Natrona County has removed more than 2,800 voters from the rolls since 2024 under HB 318 (2025) and existing inactive-voter maintenance law, with roughly 2,400 dropped for not voting in 2024 and 445 under the new statute.

DC.title: 'Younger voters tend to be a bit more receptive': DC to use ranked choice voting for the first time
DC.summary: D.C. will use ranked-choice voting for the first time in the June 16 primary, allowing voters to rank up to five candidates per race; the Board of Elections is running an education campaign focused on older voters and residents east of the Anacostia.

AL.title: Voting machines tested ahead of May 19 primary
AL.summary: Alabama election officials conducted public logic-and-accuracy testing of voting machines ahead of the May 19 primary, demonstrating that tabulators correctly read ballots.

AL.title: Voting rights groups seek emergency relief as Ivey sets special elections
AL.summary: Voting rights groups asked the federal court for emergency relief after Gov. Kay Ivey called special elections for four congressional districts using the 2023 map, arguing voters had already cast ballots under the court-ordered map.

AL.title: Election 2026: What to know before casting your primary ballot on May 19
AL.summary: A voter guide outlining polling hours, ID requirements, and races on the ballot for Alabama's May 19 primary election.

GA.title: Five things to know about the upcoming Senate election in Georgia
GA.summary: Preview of Georgia's May 19 primary focused on the crowded Republican U.S. Senate field vying to face Sen. Jon Ossoff in November, with polling showing a potential June 16 runoff.

HI.title: Hawaii sticks with its mail-in voting system despite Trump's order
HI.summary: Hawaii's chief elections officer says the state will continue mail-in voting per state law despite President Trump's executive order, as lawsuits proceed challenging the federal directive.

HI.title: 'Not Pau Yet': Bissen files for mayoral re-election, saying steady leadership is crucial
HI.summary: Maui County Mayor Richard Bissen officially filed nomination papers for re-election ahead of the August 8 primary, joining a growing field of mayoral candidates.

HI.title: Key Maui Council incumbents officially commit to race for re-election
HI.summary: Several incumbent Maui County Council members formally filed nomination papers to seek re-election in 2026, with the primary set for August 8.

IN.title: Indianapolis primary voter turnout tops last 4 midterms

IA.title: Early voting begins for Iowa's 2026 primaries: Here's what to know

MI.summary: CNN analysis of Greene's roughly 20-point win in Michigan's 35th Senate District special election, viewed as another Democratic over-performance ahead of November 2026.

MI.title: Chedwick Greene wins Michigan 35th Senate District special election
MI.summary: Saginaw fire captain Chedrick Greene defeated Republican Jason Tunney to fill the seat vacated by Kristen McDonald Rivet, who left for the U.S. House.

MI.title: Democrats keep control of Michigan state Senate after special election win
MI.summary: Democrats retained their majority in the Michigan Senate after Greene's victory in the 35th District, an outcome that keeps Gov. Gretchen Whitmer's party in control of the chamber.

MN.title: House passes elections bill after lengthy amendments discussions
MN.source: Minnesota House of Representatives - Session Daily
MN.summary: The Minnesota House passed HF4240/SF4006 by a 119-15 vote — an elections bill that strengthens election integrity, funds counties for special elections, standardizes use of the statewide voter registration system, and clarifies early voting procedures, after defeating Republican amendments to tighten voter roll rules.

MS.title: Fifth Circuit vacates order requiring Mississippi to redraw state Supreme Court districts
MS.summary: The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals vacated a lower-court order that had required Mississippi to redraw its state Supreme Court districts to remedy Voting Rights Act dilution, citing the Supreme Court's recent Louisiana v. Callais ruling.

MS.title: Gov. Reeves calls off Mississippi's special session on judicial redistricting
MS.summary: Gov. Tate Reeves canceled the May 20 special session he had called to redraw state Supreme Court districts, after the Fifth Circuit vacated the federal order that had found the existing map diluted Black voting strength.

MO.title: Wide-reaching Missouri election bill includes changes to automatic campaign donations
MO.summary: The Missouri House passed 101-47 a sweeping elections bill that bars automatic recurring campaign donations without explicit donor consent, allows candidates to use campaign funds for childcare, and sets rules for engaging voters at polling places. The bill now heads to Gov. Mike Kehoe.

MO.title: Missouri redistricting foes want Hoskins to decide on referendum now — why that’s not likely
MO.summary: Organizers seeking to overturn Missouri's new congressional map via a November 2026 referendum want Secretary of State Denny Hoskins to certify their signatures immediately, but Hoskins said he will follow the statutory timeline allowing local clerks until July 27 to verify signatures.

MT.title: Montana voters will be able to register to vote on Election Day, judge rules
MT.summary: A Montana judge blocked the state from limiting Election Day voter registration, finding the 2025 legislative change would disproportionately harm Native American and young voters. Same-day registration, in place since 2006, will remain available for the June 2 primary.

MT.title: 2026 Primary Election: Heart of Kalispell Sees Two-Way Primary Between Incumbent and Challenger for House District 7
MT.summary: Profile of the Republican primary in Montana House District 7 in Kalispell ahead of the June 2 primary, part of Flathead Beacon's contested-race coverage.

MT.title: 2026 Primary Election: Two Democratic Candidates Vie for Nomination in Senate District 8
MT.summary: Coverage of the contested Democratic primary for Montana Senate District 8 ahead of the June 2, 2026 primary election.

NE.title: Scott Petersen wins GOP primary race for Nebraska secretary of state against incumbent Bob Evnen
NE.summary: Omaha businessman Scott Petersen defeated incumbent Secretary of State Bob Evnen by more than 16,000 votes in the Republican primary, after campaigning on hand-counting ballots and restricting mail voting. He will face Democrat Sarah Slattery in November.

NE.title: Nebraska secretary of state loses GOP primary to challenger questioning election security
NE.summary: NBC News reports that Nebraska's chief election official Bob Evnen, who had called the state's elections the 'gold standard,' lost his GOP primary to challenger Scott Petersen, who questioned the state's election security practices.

NE.title: Election 2026: Gubernatorial candidates Pillen, Walz easily advance in Nebraska primary
NE.summary: Republican Gov. Jim Pillen and Democrat Lynne Walz won decisive victories in their primaries Tuesday, setting up a November gubernatorial general election matchup.

NE.title: Election 2026: Nebraska Congressional Dist. 2 Democratic race called for Denise Powell
NE.summary: Overnight returns showed Powell expanding her lead in the close Democratic primary for Nebraska's 2nd Congressional District, a swing district expected to be one of the most competitive U.S. House races in November.

NJ.title: 2026 Election Results For Newark Mayor, City Council (UPDATED)
NJ.summary: Newark held its nonpartisan municipal election on May 12, 2026, with incumbent Mayor Ras Baraka winning re-election decisively and the incumbent council slate leading their races.

NJ.title: Ashe-Nadrowski wins Bayonne mayorship
NJ.summary: In the May 12 nonpartisan municipal election, Sharon Ashe-Nadrowski won the Bayonne mayoral race outright with a roughly 65%-28% lead, becoming the city's first female mayor and avoiding a June runoff.

NM.title: Semi-open Primaries Come to NM This Election Season
NM.summary: New Mexico is using its new semi-open primary system for the first time in the June 2 primary, allowing roughly 370,000 unaffiliated voters to participate without changing their party registration.

NC.title: 34K deceased voters found on NC rolls
NC.summary: The North Carolina State Board of Elections identified approximately 34,000 deceased individuals on the state voter rolls after cross-referencing registrations with the federal SAVE database in April 2026.

OH.title: Ohio absentee ballot returns steady after deadline change
OH.summary: Initial data from Ohio's May 5 primary shows about a 90% absentee ballot return rate, comparable to past years, despite a new law eliminating the four-day grace period for mailed ballots to arrive after Election Day.

OK.title: Up to 5 state questions from Oklahoma lawmakers coming up this election season
OK.summary: Oklahoma lawmakers have advanced up to five state questions for the 2026 ballot, including a constitutional voter ID requirement (SQ 846) on the August 25 primary runoff ballot and a citizen-led minimum wage measure (SQ 832) on the June 16 primary.

OR.title: About 12% of Oregon voters have cast ballots week ahead of primary election
OR.summary: Oregon election officials have received about 357,000 ballots, roughly 12% of the 3.1 million sent to registered voters ahead of the May 19 primary, on pace with historical averages.

PA.title: Pa. primary 2026: When and where Allegheny County voters can cast their ballots
PA.summary: With Pennsylvania's primary on May 19, the Post-Gazette outlines where Allegheny County voters can return mail ballots and find polling places, noting that the mail ballot application deadline passed at 5 p.m. on May 12.

SC.title: South Carolina Senate rejects effort to tackle redistricting despite pressure from Trump
SC.summary: A resolution to extend the South Carolina legislative session to take up congressional redistricting fell short of the two-thirds support needed in the state Senate, with five Republicans joining Democrats to block the effort to redraw Rep. James Clyburn's majority-Black district before the 2026 midterms.

SC.title: Five South Carolina Republicans Who Defied Trump On Redistricting Vote
SC.summary: Five Republican state senators broke with President Trump and joined Democrats to block a resolution that would have extended the South Carolina legislative session to consider a mid-decade congressional redistricting plan.

SC.title: Sources: McMaster expected to call SC lawmakers back for special session on redistricting
SC.summary: Sources indicated Gov. Henry McMaster is expected to call South Carolina lawmakers back for a special session on congressional redistricting after the state Senate rejected an attempt to extend the regular session for that purpose.

SC.title: The State House Gavel: Senate denies White House push to redraw SC congressional map
SC.summary: Coverage of the South Carolina Senate's vote denying the White House's push to redraw the state's congressional map ahead of the 2026 midterms.

SD.title: New SD laws create 1,500 federal-only voters ahead of June 2 primary
SD.summary: New South Dakota laws have resulted in more than 1,500 voters being designated as federal-only ahead of the June 2 primary, meaning they can only vote in federal contests and not in state or local races due to expanded address and citizenship documentation requirements.

TN.title: Tennessee Democrats stripped of House committee seats over redistricting protests
TN.summary: House Speaker Cameron Sexton removed all 24 Democratic state representatives from their committee assignments as punishment for protests during the special session that approved a new congressional map dismantling a Black-majority district around Memphis.

TN.title: Tennessee House speaker suspends all Dems from committees, citing decorum violation
TN.summary: Tennessee House Speaker Cameron Sexton suspended all Democratic members from their committee assignments, citing decorum violations during the recent special session on congressional redistricting.

TN.title: Megan Barry, Other Democrats Pour Into Redrawn Congressional Races
TN.summary: Democratic congressional candidates are scrambling to adjust their 2026 campaigns after the Tennessee legislature passed a new congressional map that dismantled a Black-majority district around Memphis.

TN.title: Tennessee GOP removes Democrats from House committees over redistricting protest
TN.summary: Republican leaders in the Tennessee House removed all Democratic members from their committees, citing protest behavior during the recent special session on congressional redistricting.

TX.title: Here are primary runoffs to watch as Texas voters pick congressional nominees for November
TX.summary: Preview of the key congressional primary runoff races on the May 26 ballot, noting that with many Texas districts drawn to favor one party, primary voters will effectively be picking November’s representatives.

TX.title: With Trump and Talarico aligned on a gas tax holiday, Cornyn gets on board
TX.summary: Sen. John Cornyn, locked in a Republican primary runoff with Attorney General Ken Paxton, joined Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico and President Trump in backing a gas tax pause ahead of the May 26 runoff election.

VA.title: What does 'election' mean? One answer doomed Virginia's new congressional map
VA.summary: Analysis of how the Virginia Supreme Court's interpretation of when an 'election' begins — including the early voting period rather than only Election Day — was the key legal ruling that nullified the redistricting referendum voters approved in April.

WA.title: WA Supreme Court races shape up as income tax case looms
WA.summary: Five Washington Supreme Court seats are on the 2026 ballot — an unprecedented number — with the contests gaining attention because justices will likely decide the fate of the state’s new income tax on high earners.

WA.title: WA Supreme Court races shape up as income tax case looms
WA.summary: Five seats on the Washington Supreme Court are on the November 2026 ballot, drawing heightened attention because the court is expected to rule on the constitutionality of the state’s new income tax on high earners.

WV.title: Live coverage: 2026 West Virginia primary election
WV.summary: Coverage of West Virginia's May 13 primary election day, when voters across all 55 counties chose nominees for U.S. Senate, both congressional districts, and statewide and legislative offices.

WV.title: West Virginia Senate primary: Capito, Anderson projected winners by DDHQ
WV.summary: Incumbent Republican Sen. Shelley Moore Capito won her primary over state Sen. Tom Willis and a crowded GOP field, while Rachel Anderson won the Democratic Senate primary, setting up the November 2026 general election matchup.

WV.title: PRIMARY ELECTION RESULTS: Incumbent legislators dominate while incumbent judges are swept
WV.summary: Results from West Virginia's May 13 primary election showed incumbent state legislators winning their primaries broadly, while several sitting judges lost their races.

WV.title: West Virginia primary election results for U.S. Senate, U.S. House and more
WV.summary: Statewide primary election results for U.S. Senate, U.S. House, governor, and other West Virginia races on the May 13 primary ballot.

WI.title: Wisconsin Republicans look to Donald Trump's die-hard fans to brighten their prospects in November
WI.summary: At the Wisconsin GOP's state convention in the Dells, party leaders sought to energize Trump's base ahead of November, while polling shows the president's standing softening among Wisconsin voters following the April state Supreme Court loss.

WY.title: Registered to vote? Clerks purge voter rolls of thousands; party affiliation deadline is Wednesday
WY.summary: Wyoming county clerks have purged thousands of inactive voters under a 2025 law, and registered voters face a May 13 deadline to declare or change party affiliation ahead of the closed August primary.

WY.title: Wyomingites must declare a political party by tomorrow. Here’s how
WY.summary: Explainer on Wyoming's May 13 deadline for voters to declare or change their party affiliation in order to participate in the August primary under the state's closed-primary system.

AK.title: Democratic group plans to spend $10M on TV ads in Alaska's U.S. Senate race
AK.summary: The Democratic Senate Majority PAC is reserving $10 million in Alaska TV advertising to support Democratic challenger Mary Peltola against incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in a race that will be decided under Alaska's top-four ranked-choice voting system in November.

AZ.title: Maricopa County's election IT fight isn't about IT. It's about democracy.
AZ.summary: An ongoing legal battle between Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap and the county board of supervisors over control of election infrastructure—including ballot drop boxes and early ballot processing—is raising concerns about who will administer the state's largest county's elections in 2026.

AZ.title: Recorder Heap Victorious Again in Battle with Maricopa County Supervisors
AZ.summary: An Arizona Superior Court denied the Maricopa County Board of Supervisors' Motion to Stay, further cementing County Recorder Justin Heap's authority over key election operations including ballot drop boxes and early vote processing ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

AR.title: Sanders appoints special justice to hear election case filed against her; Democratic Party opposes
AR.summary: The Arkansas Democratic Party is opposing Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders' appointment of a special justice to the Arkansas Supreme Court to hear an election case filed against her, raising concerns about impartiality in a legal matter directly involving the sitting governor.

AR.title: Super PACs spend $2.3 million total on Arkansas' U.S. Senate race to boost Cotton, attack Shoffner
AR.summary: Two super PACs have reported $2.3 million in combined independent expenditures in Arkansas's U.S. Senate race, with spending concentrated on supporting incumbent Tom Cotton and attacking Democratic Senate candidate Hallie Shoffner ahead of the November general election.

CA.title: California Democrats think voting late will stop a GOP sweep. They might slow down the results
CA.summary: Some California Democratic voters are strategically waiting until late in the June 2 primary to cast ballots in hopes of monitoring polling trends before choosing a gubernatorial candidate, a tactic election officials warn could delay results in the already crowded race with 61 candidates.

CO.title: Move over Election Day. Colorado is about to start having election month.
CO.summary: HB 1113 awaiting Governor Polis' signature would extend Colorado's ballot mailing window and add new election safeguards, including emergency voting rules if major disruptions occur, and prohibits persons convicted of election offenses from serving as election watchers.

CT.title: Luke Bronin beats John Larson in convention upset, faces primary
CT.summary: Former Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin won the Democratic endorsement for Connecticut's 1st Congressional District at the party convention, defeating 14-term incumbent John Larson and setting up an August primary under Connecticut's newly expanded absentee and early voting rules.

FL.title: Judge takes step to consolidate redistricting challenges ahead of hearing to put Florida map on hold
FL.summary: A Leon County circuit judge moved to consolidate three lawsuits challenging Florida's new congressional redistricting map signed by Gov. DeSantis, with a hearing set to consider blocking the map before the 2026 midterms. Plaintiffs argue the redrawn map violates Florida's Fair Districts constitutional amendment.

FL.title: 'Petition accomplished': Here are the 2026 candidates who qualified for the ballot by petition
FL.summary: Florida Politics tracks candidates who qualified for the 2026 general election ballot by petition, including several local races ahead of the August 18 primary, explaining how Florida's petition-qualifying process works and which candidates have met the signature threshold.

GA.title: 6 candidates qualify in special election to replace late Rep. David Scott in Congress
GA.summary: Six candidates, including Rep. Scott's daughter Marcye Scott, qualified for the July 28 special election to fill Georgia's 13th congressional district seat left vacant by Scott's death, with a runoff on August 25 if no candidate wins a majority.

HI.title: Hawaii sticks with its mail-in voting system despite Trump's order
HI.summary: Hawaii election officials say the state will continue its mandatory mail-in voting system for the 2026 elections despite President Trump's executive order targeting mail ballots, with the state elections officer saying a change would require new legislation. Hawaii has joined a 19-state coalition suing the Trump administration over the order.

ID.title: It's not clear if Idaho district judge candidate in Ada County is legally qualified for the role
ID.summary: An Ada County judicial candidate in Idaho's May 19 primary appears to fall months short of the state's 10-year bar admission requirement, raising questions about ballot eligibility days before the election and broader concerns about candidate vetting.

IL.title: How Illinois county clerks are combating election misinformation
IL.summary: Illinois county clerks and state election officials describe their proactive strategies for countering voting misinformation ahead of the 2026 midterms, including monitoring social media with state police and DHS. Officials across party lines say transparency and rapid response have helped address declining voter confidence in election security.

IN.title: GOP Sen. Deery's lead firms up to 3 votes over Trump-backed challenger
IN.summary: State Sen. Spencer Deery extended his lead to three votes over Trump-endorsed challenger Paula Copenhaver after Parke County verified a provisional ballot, though two more provisional ballots in Tippecanoe County remain. The ultra-close Indiana Senate District 23 result may still trigger a formal recount petition.

IN.title: Indiana's Senate District 23 race could come down to a single vote
IN.summary: With provisional ballots still being counted in Tippecanoe County, the Indiana Senate District 23 Republican primary margin could shrink to a single vote. Candidates have until May 19 noon to file a recount petition in a race that has drawn national attention.

IN.title: SOS Morales asked to step aside if recount occurs, criticized for D.C. trip
IN.summary: A Democratic state legislator called on Indiana Secretary of State Diego Morales to recuse himself from any potential recount of the Senate District 23 primary race, citing concerns about impartiality after he attended a White House event during the vote-counting period. Morales' office declined.

IN.title: Indiana Sec. of State's office outlines recount, contest petition process following primary election
IN.summary: Indiana's Secretary of State office clarified the recount and contest petition process after the May 5 primary, explaining there are no automatic recounts and candidates have until May 19 to file. The explainer is directly relevant to the ongoing Senate District 23 race decided by three votes.

IA.title: Iowa Democrats face a competitive primary as they attempt to flip Ernst's open Senate seat
IA.summary: Iowa Public Radio profiles the Democratic Senate primary between Josh Turek and Zach Wahls as early voting opens, with both candidates competing to flip the seat vacated by retiring Sen. Joni Ernst and a televised debate scheduled for May 14 evening.

IA.title: Democrats Will Debate in Iowa US Senate Primary Shaped by Outside Money and Big-Name Endorsements
IA.summary: Turek and Wahls face off in a televised debate on May 14 as VoteVets spends $7 million supporting Turek; the open-seat race features major endorsements from Sen. Warren and Pete Buttigieg ahead of Iowa's June 2 primary.

KY.title: No-excuse early voting begins in Kentucky
KY.summary: No-excuse in-person early voting opened statewide in Kentucky on May 14 for the May 19 primary, running through Saturday May 16 and covering races including the open U.S. Senate seat vacated by Mitch McConnell.

KY.title: Voting in the Kentucky primary? Early voting polls open May 14
KY.summary: Early voting opened May 14 for Kentucky's May 19 primary, with the Secretary of State noting more early voting locations than in November 2024; 12 Republicans and 7 Democrats are competing for McConnell's Senate seat.

KY.title: Early voting for Kentucky primary elections begins Thursday
KY.summary: The Kentucky Lantern reports that no-excuse absentee early voting began Thursday, May 14, ahead of the May 19 primary, with polling at county clerks' offices and designated satellite locations statewide through Saturday May 16.

LA.title: Louisiana redistricting fight heads to full Senate vote
LA.summary: Louisiana's full Senate took up a new congressional map on May 14 that would eliminate one majority-Black district and give Republicans a 5-1 House advantage, following the Supreme Court ruling that struck down the state's prior map.

LA.title: Louisiana senators take up new US House map while South Carolina plans for extra redistricting work
LA.summary: The Louisiana Senate considered a redistricting bill that would dissolve Rep. Cleo Fields' majority-Black 6th District; the measure must pass both chambers by June 1 before suspended House primaries can be rescheduled.

LA.title: Who's winning the 2026 redistricting war? Not voters
LA.summary: NPR examines how Louisiana's suspension of congressional primaries — invalidating tens of thousands of already-cast absentee ballots — is fueling voter cynicism, with advocates warning the instability reinforces the perception that elections are rigged.

LA.title: A majority-Black district in Louisiana traces a long fight over the Voting Rights Act
LA.summary: In-depth account of Louisiana's 6th Congressional District and decades-long legal battles over majority-Black representation that culminated in the April 2026 Supreme Court ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act, prompting the current redistricting fight.

ME.title: JD Vance expected to address anti-fraud efforts during Bangor visit
ME.summary: Vice President Vance traveled to Bangor on May 14 to highlight the Trump administration's election-fraud investigations ahead of Maine's June 9 primary, also campaigning for Republican 2nd-district congressional candidate Paul LePage.

MD.title: Maryland passes first state law including ranked choice voting
MD.summary: Governor Wes Moore signed SB848/HB1448 on May 12, marking the first time ranked choice voting has been written into Maryland law; the bipartisan bill sets new election administration requirements for RCV elections in Maryland cities.

MA.title: Amid a deluge of ballot questions, Massachusetts' high court could dramatically shape the November ballot
MA.summary: The Massachusetts SJC is weighing legal challenges to multiple 2026 ballot initiatives on a compressed timeline, including the all-party primary proposal that would eliminate party primaries and reshape how voters participate in Massachusetts elections.

MI.title: After MI Senate special election, what's ahead for Legislature and November midterms?
MI.summary: Following Democrat Chedrick Greene's decisive win in the Michigan Senate District 35 special election, this piece examines what the restored 20-18 Democratic majority means for the legislative session and what the result signals for November midterms in a competitive state.

MI.title: Democratic U.S. Senate candidates escalate attacks as Michigan primary intensifies
MI.summary: With Michigan's August 4 primary approaching, the three-way Democratic contest for the U.S. Senate seat has grown sharply contested in a state considered a key Senate battleground.

MI.title: Your 2026 Michigan voting guide
MI.summary: A comprehensive guide covering Michigan's 2026 election calendar, voter registration rules (including Election Day registration), absentee voting procedures, and key statewide races including governor, U.S. Senate, and all 13 congressional districts.

MS.title: Democrats get a last-minute reprieve on 2026 redistricting
MS.summary: Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves canceled a planned special session to redraw state Supreme Court voting districts after the 5th Circuit vacated the redistricting order, giving Black Democratic incumbents a temporary reprieve while the governor signaled plans to pursue congressional redistricting after the midterms.

MO.title: Missouri's new congressional map is set. Who's running for Kansas City's 5th District?
MO.summary: Following the Missouri Supreme Court's unanimous ruling upholding the GOP-gerrymandered congressional map, this report examines the crowded candidate field in the redrawn 5th District—where incumbent Rep. Emanuel Cleaver faces six Republican challengers—ahead of the August 4 primary.

MO.title: Missouri redistricting foes want Hoskins to decide on referendum now. Here's why that's not likely
MO.summary: People Not Politicians is pressing Secretary of State Denny Hoskins to certify referendum petition signatures and suspend the gerrymandered congressional map, but Hoskins has until August 4 to verify signatures—the same day as the primary—creating potential legal chaos around Missouri elections.

MT.title: 2026 Primary Election: Incumbent Challenged for Republican Nomination in House District 13
MT.summary: With absentee ballots already mailed and Montana's June 2 primary underway under new voter ID rules, incumbent Rep. Linda Reksten faces a primary challenger in House District 13 amid GOP intraparty conflict over her voting record on Medicaid expansion and nonpartisan courts.

NE.title: Denise Powell wins Democratic primary for battleground Nebraska seat
NE.summary: Political organizer Denise Powell defeated State Sen. John Cavanaugh by about 2 percentage points to win the Nebraska 2nd District Democratic primary, setting up a competitive general election against Republican Brinker Harding in Omaha's 'blue dot' district seen as a key House battleground.

NE.title: Denise Powell wins Democratic primary for Nebraska's 2nd congressional district
NE.summary: The AP called the Nebraska NE-02 Democratic primary for Denise Powell in a close six-person race in an Omaha-area district considered one of Democrats' top opportunities to flip a House seat in the 2026 midterms.

NV.title: Why Nevadans should care about the Supreme Court dismantling protections for fair representation of Black voters
NV.summary: Nevada officials and advocates warn that the Supreme Court's 6-3 ruling gutting Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act threatens fair electoral representation in Nevada, where voters of color make up more than 50% of the electorate in three of the state's four congressional districts.

NV.title: Nevada Secretary of State gives voter roll update ahead of midterm primaries
NV.summary: Nevada Secretary of State Francisco Aguilar reported that spring voter roll maintenance designated 119,533 voters inactive and canceled 7,583 registrations, with early voting for the June 9 primary set to begin May 23.

NJ.title: Newark Mayor Ras Baraka Wins The Mayoral Race
NJ.summary: Ras Baraka won re-election as Newark mayor with over 70% of the vote in New Jersey's largest city's nonpartisan May 12 municipal election, securing a fourth term over seven challengers.

NJ.title: Baraka wins fourth term as Newark mayor
NJ.summary: New Jersey Globe reports that Baraka captured 70.34% of the vote in Newark's nonpartisan municipal election, decisively defeating seven opponents in the city's most-watched 2026 local election.

NY.title: NY Elections, Census and Redistricting Update 05/11/26
NY.summary: CityLand's weekly elections update covers New York's mid-decade redistricting push after the Supreme Court weakened the Voting Rights Act, including proposed constitutional amendments to allow the legislature to redraw congressional maps before 2028.

NY.title: Redistricting war isn't over, Democrats say as Jeffries calls a meeting this week
NY.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called New York among states expected to respond to the Supreme Court's Voting Rights Act ruling with a 'massive Democratic redistricting counteroffensive,' directly affecting how New York's congressional voters will be represented.

NC.title: North Carolina voters have until July to comment on proposed election rules
NC.summary: The North Carolina State Board of Elections opened public comment through July 14 on four sets of proposed administrative rules covering absentee voting procedures, photo ID requirements for mail-in ballots, recount processes, and voting site administration.

NC.title: North Carolina Senate Primary 2026 Live Results: Cooper, Whatley Win
NC.summary: Former Gov. Roy Cooper and former RNC Chair Michael Whatley won their May 12 runoff primaries, setting up a high-profile U.S. Senate general election battle for North Carolina's open seat expected to be a key race for Senate control.

ND.title: What to know before the June 9 primary election in North Dakota
ND.summary: A comprehensive voter guide for North Dakota's June 9 primary covers two constitutional ballot measures on term limits and initiative petition rules, more than 765 positions on the ballot, and new mail-in ballot rules requiring ballots to be received by Election Day.

OH.title: Catching Our Eye News Roundup, May 13, 2026
OH.summary: Post-primary roundup covers the emerging November matchup between Vivek Ramaswamy and Amy Acton for governor, analysis of school levy failures at the May 5 primary, and expert commentary on whether Ohio is returning to battleground status given tight polling in governor and Senate races.

OR.title: Today is the last preferred day to return ballots by mail in Oregon. What to do after
OR.summary: Oregon election officials warned that May 14 is the last recommended day to mail ballots for the May 19 primary due to U.S. Postal Service delivery concerns, advising voters who miss the window to use official drop boxes or request a manual USPS postmark.

RI.title: Supreme Court voting rights ruling set to reshape local power from statehouses to school boards

Callais decision weakening the Voting Rights Act, noting Rhode Island is among at least 10 states that introduced their own state-level voting rights bills this year in response to eroding federal protections.

SC.title: S.C. governor calls special session for redistricting despite concerns

James Clyburn's district and give Republicans an advantage in all seven U.S. House seats.

SC.title: South Carolina Governor Plans Special Session to Redraw House Maps
SC.summary: Gov. McMaster's special session announcement came after the Senate failed a 29-17 vote to extend the regular session; a new map could shift South Carolina's June 9 congressional primaries to August and would favor Republicans across all seven districts.

TN.title: Who's winning the 2026 redistricting war? Not voters
TN.summary: NPR examines the wave of mid-decade redistricting following the Supreme Court's voting rights ruling, including how Tennessee's newly enacted congressional map splitting the state's only majority-Black, Democrat-held Memphis district into three affects voters amid ongoing federal court challenges.

TN.title: NAACP alleges new Tennessee congressional map intentionally discriminates on basis of race
TN.summary: The NAACP filed a federal civil rights lawsuit arguing Tennessee's redrawn congressional map deliberately cracks Memphis's majority-Black district across three districts to dilute Black voting power in violation of the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments, with a federal court hearing scheduled for May 20.

TX.title: Will Texas get another MAGA attorney general? Or something new?
TX.summary: Ahead of the May 26 Republican primary runoff, this report examines the Texas attorney general race—one of the most-watched contests—where candidates compete to succeed Ken Paxton, with early voting starting May 18.

UT.title: Redrawn district, narrow convention margin set up competitive House Republican primary in Utah
UT.summary: Under Utah's newly court-ordered congressional map, incumbent Rep. Celeste Maloy narrowly beat Phil Lyman at the Republican convention and now faces him again in the June 23 primary, setting up one of the most competitive House races in the state's history.

VT.title: Vermont's U.S. Rep. Becca Balint announces reelection campaign
VT.summary: Rep. Becca Balint officially launched her reelection bid for Vermont's sole U.S. House seat, setting up a rematch with Republican Mark Coester ahead of the August 11 primary and November general election.

VA.title: SCOTUS is dismantling voting rights, but Virginia offers examples of a way forward
VA.summary: In the wake of a U.S. Supreme Court ruling weakening the Voting Rights Act, Virginia leaders warn that minority representation could erode under future Republican-controlled redistricting, while pointing to Virginia's 2021 state Voting Rights Act as a model for protecting voters.

WV.title: Primary Election Post Mortem

WI.title: Wisconsin GOP looks to Trump's die-hard fans to brighten election prospects
WI.source: Wisconsin Watch / Milwaukee Neighborhood News Service

DC.title: DC Mayor Race 2026 — Candidate Tracker
DC.summary: With DC's June 16 primary ballots now in the mail and ranked choice voting being used for the first time in DC history, this tracker profiles all seven candidates competing in the open mayoral race following Mayor Muriel Bowser's retirement.

AL.title: Election Day: What to bring to vote in Alabama's May 19 primary
AL.summary: Alabama voters heading to the polls for the May 19 statewide primary must present a valid photo ID; the article outlines accepted forms of identification and explains provisional ballot options for voters without ID, ahead of a primary that also involves ongoing redistricting uncertainty for four congressional districts.

FL.title: Judge to hear challenge to new congressional districts
FL.summary: A Leon County circuit court judge was set to hear arguments from plaintiffs challenging Florida's newly signed congressional redistricting map, which critics say violates the state's Fair Districts constitutional amendments and is designed to give Republicans four additional seats.

FL.title: Florida judge to hear consolidation arguments in state redistricting lawsuits
FL.summary: A Leon County circuit judge heard arguments on consolidating three separate lawsuits seeking to block Florida's new congressional map, with plaintiffs arguing it violates the Fair Districts amendments voters adopted in 2010 to curb partisan gerrymandering and protect minority voting rights.

GA.title: Early voting ends today in Georgia's Democratic, GOP primaries
GA.summary: Georgia's early in-person voting period concluded on May 15 ahead of the May 19 primary election, with more than 700,000 voters having already cast ballots — a roughly 28% increase over the comparable point in the 2022 primary cycle.

GA.title: Georgia early voting ends Friday as turnout surges ahead of 2026 primary election
GA.summary: The final day of Georgia's early voting period drew record-breaking participation ahead of the May 19 primary, driven by competitive statewide races for governor, secretary of state, and a crowded Republican contest for the U.S. Senate seat held by Jon Ossoff.

GA.title: Georgia election 2026: Early voting ends Friday for primary elections
GA.summary: WSB-TV reported on the close of Georgia's early voting window on May 15 and provided voter guidance on polling locations and rules for the upcoming May 19 primary, noting turnout was outpacing 2022 levels significantly.

HI.title: Judge weighs Democrats' bid to block Trump's executive order on voting
HI.summary: A federal judge heard arguments from Democratic Party lawyers seeking to block Trump's March 31 executive order on elections, which would restrict mail-in voting and require citizenship proof to register — Hawaii, which operates an all-mail voting system under state law, joined 19 other attorneys general in suing to block the order.

ID.title: Friday is the deadline to early vote in Idaho ahead of 2026 primary election
ID.summary: Idaho's early in-person absentee voting window closes May 15 ahead of the May 19 primary; voters who missed the early voting or pre-registration deadlines can still register and cast a ballot in person on Election Day with valid photo ID and proof of residence.

ID.title: Friday is the deadline to early vote in Idaho
ID.summary: The Coeur d'Alene Press reminded north Idaho voters that May 15 is the last day for early in-person voting before Idaho's May 19 primary election, which features contested races for governor, both U.S. House seats, and a U.S. Senate seat.

IL.title: Right-wing group sues Illinois in first post-Callais attack on a state Voting Rights Act
IL.summary: The Public Interest Legal Foundation filed a federal lawsuit seeking to strike down Illinois' Voting Rights Act, arguing it unconstitutionally uses race as a primary factor in drawing legislative maps, in what Democracy Docket calls the first direct challenge to a state-level voting rights act following the U.S. Supreme Court's Callais ruling.

LA.title: Louisiana Senate approves new map that would scrap majority-Black district
LA.summary: The Louisiana Senate passed a new congressional map eliminating one of the state's two majority-Black districts, shifting the state's delegation from a 4-2 to a 5-1 Republican advantage following the Supreme Court's Callais decision invalidating race-based district drawing.

MN.title: House Approves Final Elections Committee Bills
MN.source: Minnesota House of Representatives Session Daily
MN.summary: The Minnesota House gave final approval to two elections bills (HF4239 and HF4240), voting to concur with Senate amendments and sending them to Governor Walz for signature; the bills modernize election administration, streamline procedures, and standardize use of the statewide voter registration system.

MO.title: Missouri's gerrymandered map sows electoral confusion
MO.summary: Following the Missouri Supreme Court's unanimous ruling upholding the GOP-drawn congressional map, election officials remain in limbo as the Secretary of State has not yet opened the voter registration system to reflect new district boundaries ahead of the August primary.

MO.title: Missouri map confusion leaves Jackson County, local election officials in limbo
MO.summary: Missouri's newly upheld gerrymandered congressional map splits Kansas City into three districts, leaving Jackson County and local clerks unable to update voter rolls while a referendum petition that could still block the map remains pending.

MS.title: Mississippi redistricting debate continues despite canceled special session
MS.summary: After Gov. Tate Reeves canceled the planned special session to redraw Mississippi's judicial districts, advocacy groups including the Mississippi Center for Justice announced a May 20 day of action and vowed to continue fighting any redistricting that would dilute Black voting power.

NH.title: Under new law, NH's state primary election to move up to June starting in 2028
NH.summary: Governor Kelly Ayotte signed a law moving New Hampshire's state primary from September to the second Tuesday in June beginning in 2028. Supporters say the earlier date gives non-incumbent candidates more time to campaign before the general election.

NH.title: Under new law, NH's state primary election to move up to June starting in 2028
NH.summary: Valley News coverage of New Hampshire's newly signed law shifting the state primary to the second Tuesday in June starting in 2028, noting Secretary of State David Scanlan's commitment to executing the new schedule despite having favored an August primary date.

NJ.title: Insider NJ's 2026 Nonpartisan May Municipal Elections Publication
NJ.summary: Post-election coverage of New Jersey's May 12 nonpartisan municipal elections, reporting results including Mayor André Sayegh's reelection in Paterson and the Newark mayoral race, conducted under the state's newly expanded early voting law for May municipal contests.

NM.title: Semi-open primary in New Mexico enables more participation
NM.summary: New Mexico's June 2 primary is the state's first semi-open primary under Senate Bill 16, allowing over 330,000 unaffiliated 'decline to state' voters to request a Democratic or Republican ballot without changing their party registration, a historic expansion of primary participation.

NY.title: Hakeem Jeffries pushes New York to join redistricting battle
NY.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries dispatched Rep. Joe Morelle to Albany to lobby for a mid-decade redistricting constitutional amendment in response to the Supreme Court's Voting Rights Act decision, arguing it is necessary to protect minority voting representation in congressional maps.

NY.title: Gianaris: Chances of passing budget next week 'very slim' as negotiations mesh with redistricting push
NY.summary: Deputy Senate Majority Leader Mike Gianaris and Assembly Speaker Carl Heastie confirmed New York will advance a constitutional amendment potentially enabling mid-decade redistricting as a response to GOP map-drawing in red states, though the amendment would not affect election maps before 2028.

PA.title: Pa. primary election 2026: What you need to know before you vote
PA.summary: Comprehensive voter guide for Pennsylvania's May 19 primary covering registration status, mail ballot deadlines, closed primary rules, and key statewide races including governor and all 17 congressional districts.

PA.title: Pennsylvania voting rights: what to know for May 19 election
PA.summary: Outlines voter rights for Pennsylvania's May 19 primary including ID requirements only for first-time voters at a polling location, provisional ballot access, and protections flowing from recent Pennsylvania Supreme Court rulings on flawed mail ballots.

PA.title: Your last-minute guide to voting in the 2026 PA primary election
PA.summary: Last-minute voting guide for Pennsylvania's May 19 primary covering polling hours, ballot return deadlines, how to find your polling place, and an overview of statewide races on the ballot.

PA.title: What you need to know about voter intimidation in Pennsylvania
PA.summary: Explains state and federal laws prohibiting voter intimidation in Pennsylvania ahead of the May 19 primary, including how voters can report incidents to county election offices and the Office of the Attorney General.

SC.title: The State House Gavel: Gov orders lawmakers to return for special session to take up redistricting
SC.summary: Gov. McMaster ordered the South Carolina legislature back for a special session on May 15 to attempt to redraw congressional maps and eliminate the state's only majority-Black district held by Rep. Jim Clyburn, after the Senate blocked a supermajority procedural vote during the regular session.

SC.title: South Carolina redistricting: Governor forces lawmakers back to session to eliminate lone majority-Black district
SC.summary: Gov. McMaster invoked executive authority to reconvene the South Carolina legislature for a redistricting special session aimed at dismantling the state's sole Democratic congressional seat, part of a broader GOP push following the Supreme Court's weakening of Voting Rights Act protections.

SC.title: South Carolina governor calls special session on redistricting
SC.summary: CBS News covers South Carolina's governor calling a special legislative session to enact a new congressional map that would give Republicans all seven congressional seats and eliminate Rep. James Clyburn's majority-minority district ahead of the November 2026 midterms.

TN.title: Challengers seek restraining orders for new voting map as US House candidate deadline approaches
TN.summary: Multiple civil rights organizations — including the ACLU and NAACP — sought temporary restraining orders on May 15 to block Tennessee's new congressional map that eliminates the state's only majority-Black district in Memphis, as the U.S. House candidate qualification deadline arrived.

TX.title: Early voting in Texas' primary runoff election begins May 18. Here's what to know.
TX.summary: With May 15 as the mail-ballot application deadline and early voting set to begin May 18, Texas voters prepare for the May 26 primary runoff featuring the high-profile U.S. Senate race between incumbent John Cornyn and Attorney General Ken Paxton.

TX.title: Texas Secretary of State Encourages Voters to Review Official Information ahead of the May 26 Primary Runoff Election
TX.summary: Texas Secretary of State Jane Nelson issued official guidance ahead of the May 26 runoff, reminding voters that early voting runs May 18-22, that May 15 is the last day to request a mail ballot, and that photo ID is required at all polling locations.

VA.title: NAACP asks U.S. Supreme Court to overturn Virginia redistricting decision
VA.summary: The NAACP filed a brief supporting Virginia Democrats' emergency appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court to overturn the Virginia Supreme Court's May 8 ruling that voided the voters' approval of a redistricting referendum, arguing the ruling discarded over 3.1 million ballots.

VT.title: Vermont constitutional amendment on equal protection of the law headed to November ballot
VT.summary: The Vermont House voted 128-14 on May 13 to send Proposal 4, a constitutional amendment on equal protection, to the November 2026 ballot — part of the state's legislative response to the Supreme Court's weakening of federal voting rights protections.

WA.title: Bill strengthening protections on Washington's voter database takes effect
WA.summary: A new Washington law making it a felony for election officials to disclose private voter data — enacted in response to the Trump administration's 2025 request for the state's complete voter rolls — took effect, with only the Secretary of State's office authorized to respond to voter database requests.

WI.title: Wisconsin will likely see limited, local effects from Voting Rights Act ruling — at least for now
WI.summary: Wisconsin will face limited immediate fallout from the Supreme Court's Voting Rights Act ruling, though Milwaukee-area local district boundaries and future redistricting battles could be affected as progressive groups continue legal challenges to the state's congressional map.

WI.title: Wisconsin plays role in national redistricting fights
WI.summary: Wisconsin is a focal point in national redistricting litigation, with progressive law firm Law Forward vowing to appeal a court dismissal of a challenge to the state's Republican-gerrymandered congressional map to the state Supreme Court, which now has a 5-2 liberal majority.

WY.title: Wyoming voters face looming deadline for party affiliation changes
WY.summary: Wyoming voters had until 5 p.m. on May 13 to change their party registration before the primary election under Wyoming's crossover voting restrictions, after which changes cannot be made until after the August 18 primary.
